en: It's for me; Ser marks identity or an inherent trait; for a state or a place Spanish switches to estar.
Is he here?; Estar covers location and passing states so it is the verb for where something is right now.
I'm fine; Feelings and conditions take estar; soy bien is wrong even though English uses one verb for both.
He still hasn't; Ha is haber for él/ella/usted and can never stand alone — a participle must follow as in ha comido.
Let's go already!; Ir in the nosotros form doubles as the let's-go command so it works as both statement and push.
Is there anything?; Hay is impersonal and invariable — hay muchas cosas stays hay and never becomes han.
I don't have anything; Tener yo form; stacking no with nada is required rather than a double negative mistake.
How are you?; The tú form of estar asking about mood or health; ¿cómo eres? would ask what kind of person you are.
I don't know why; Saber has the irregular yo sé for facts and information; the accent separates it from the pronoun se.
I already have; He is haber for yo and only works as an auxiliary — it needs a participle like hecho or visto behind it.
It has to be me; The infinitive of ser; use it for who or what something is rather than how it feels.
He has something of mine; Tiene is tener for él/ella and is also the polite form you use with usted.
I can't take any more; Poder yo form is irregular; no puedo más is the set way to say you are at your limit.
I don't want anything else; Querer yo form; with a person querer shifts from wanting to loving.
I don't know what to do; Hacer covers both do and make so Spanish never distinguishes the two.
It was all because of you; Fue is the preterite of ser and also of ir so context decides between was and went.
Thanks for everything; Gracias is always plural and feminine; the singular gracia means grace or a joke.
Not again; Vez is feminine and its plural is veces; una vez means once and dos veces twice.
He used to be like that; Era is the imperfect of ser for how things once were with no clear end point.
I'm not like that; Soy is the irregular yo of ser for identity and character rather than a passing mood.
Are they for me?; Son is ser for ellos and also the form you use with ustedes.
What have you got there?; Tienes is tener for tú so it fits a friend but never usted.
I think so; Creer is believe or think an opinion; creo que sí is the standard yes-probably reply.
I'm on my way there now; Voy is the irregular yo of ir and the plain present already covers the near future.
Do you know anything about him?; Saber is knowing facts while conocer is being acquainted with a person.
It was here earlier; Estaba is the imperfect of estar for a background situation with no defined end.
Could that be?; Puede is poder for él/ella/usted and puede ser is the everyday way to say maybe.
You're just like that; Eres is ser for tú describing character; estás would describe today's mood instead.
That isn't true; Verdad is feminine and tacked onto a sentence as ¿verdad? it becomes the tag right?.
Let's go to my place; Casa is feminine and in the fixed phrase en casa it drops the article.
I don't have time; Tiempo is masculine and also means weather so hace buen tiempo is about the sky.
How's everything going?; Va is ir for él/ella/usted; with things it means how they are going rather than movement.
Please don't; Favor is masculine and por favor is fixed with por and never with para.
What do you want from me?; Quieres is querer for tú; said of a person it means you love them.
I'm very sorry; Siento is sentir to feel and the lo is obligatory in the apology.
Is the gentleman here?; Señor is Mr or sir and pairs with usted; before a name it takes el as in el señor García.
A long time ago; Hace is hacer for él/ella and with a time span it means ago.
You have to do something; Has is haber for tú; has de plus infinitive is obligation and sounds Spanish rather than Latin American.
What do you mean?; Decir is say or tell and querer decir is the idiom for to mean.
We have to do something; Tenemos is tener for nosotros and tener que is the ordinary way to say must.
Where is everybody?; Están is estar for ellos and ustedes and it is the form for location.
Can you do that?; Puedes is poder for tú covering both being able to and being allowed to.
I can't see anything; Ver is passive seeing while mirar is deliberately looking at something.
Oh come on!; Hombre is a man but thrown into speech in Spain it works as a nudge like come on.
That's life; Vida is feminine and mi vida is a common term of endearment for a partner or child.
There are lots of things; Cosas is the plural of the feminine cosa; one thing is una cosa.
I have to go; Ir is wildly irregular once conjugated and ir a plus infinitive is the going-to future.
I'm ten years old; Age uses tener not ser; año is masculine and the ñ matters since ano is anus.
I want to be here; The infinitive estar is for states and location; ser would claim identity instead.
All day; Día is masculine despite ending in a and buenos días is plural as a greeting.
I can't tonight; Noche is feminine (la noche) and esta noche is the normal way to say tonight; the plural buenas noches works as both hello and goodbye after dark.
We're here now; Estar we-form present for location and passing states; somos would claim identity instead.
I agree with you; Masculine noun used in the fixed phrase estar de acuerdo con alguien; on its own ¡De acuerdo! is simply OK.
I don't have a job; Masculine noun covering both job and work; spelled identically to trabajo meaning I work; context alone separates them.
Sounds good to me; Parecer he/she/usted present; me parece is how Spanish says I think; parecerse a is to resemble someone.
There are a lot of people here; Feminine and grammatically singular even though English people is plural; say la gente es amable and never son.
Whatever works is fine; Present subjunctive of ser for él/usted; lo que sea is whatever; it appears after cuando and para que where English keeps a plain verb.
My father isn't in; Masculine; the plural padres normally means parents of both sexes; in Mexican slang padre also means great.
Look at this; Tú imperative of mirar; with usted it becomes mire; in speech it is often just a filler like hey or listen.
Who said that?; Decir he/she/usted preterite built on the irregular stem dij- with no accent; the regular form dició does not exist.
What do you want?; Querer he/she/usted present with the e to ie stem change; querer a una persona means to love them.
It could be; Conditional of poder shared by yo and él; the polite way to ask favours and to hedge a guess.
I want to talk to you; Infinitive; you speak con someone and de a topic; hablar a alguien sounds like addressing rather than chatting.
Where are you going?; Ir tú present from a wholly irregular verb; vas a plus infinitive is the everyday future much like English going to.
What's going on?; Pasar he/she/it present; it stretches over to happen and to pass by and to spend time.
They have to talk to me; Haber they/ustedes present; normally the perfect auxiliary as in han hablado while haber de plus infinitive is a formal obligation.
Do you have any money?; Masculine and uncountable so there is no plural and no un dinero; amounts take algo de dinero.
I want to see the world; Masculine; the set phrase todo el mundo means everybody rather than the entire planet.
One moment please; Masculine; en este momento is right now and por el momento means for the time being.
Can I have one?; The infinitive behind tengo and tienes; tener que plus infinitive is the main way to say have to.
I have been here; Past participle of estar and also a masculine noun meaning state; after haber a participle never changes for gender or number.
There were a lot of people; Impersonal there was or there were; always singular no matter how many things follow since it is the past of hay.
He didn't have any money; Tener imperfect and the same form for yo and él so a pronoun is often needed; the imperfect suits lasting past situations.
And your mother?; Feminine; to her face most people say mamá and madre turns up in some very strong Mexican insults.
Okay see you tomorrow; Vale is Spain's all-purpose okay from valer to be worth while Latin America prefers bueno or dale.
What place is this?; Masculine; en lugar de means instead of and tener lugar means to take place.
What are you doing?; Gerund of hacer on the irregular stem haci-; it only pairs with estar and never acts as a noun the way English doing does.
Nobody knows anything; Saber he/she/usted present with its odd yo form sé; saber is knowing facts while conocer is being acquainted with people or places.
We can go tomorrow; Poder we-form present; the o to ue change of puedo drops out in nosotros.
Hold on a second; Both the he/she present and the tú command of esperar which means wait and hope and expect all at once.
What became of him?; Past participle of ser and invariable after haber; there is no form serido.
That's something else; Feminine singular of the plural cosas you already know; alguna cosa is a wordier algo and la cosa es que means the thing is.
How is your son?; Masculine with hija for a girl; the plural hijos covers children of both sexes and hijo is also warm address to a young person.
What kind of man?; Masculine; tipo de is the standard kind of and on its own tipo is a casual guy or bloke.
Are you his friend?; Masculine with amiga for a woman; unlike English boyfriend it implies nothing romantic since that is novio.
Who is that woman?; Feminine; it doubles as wife so mi mujer usually means my wife rather than my woman.
Mom I'm coming; The accent puts the stress on the last syllable and is obligatory since mama without it means breast.
Is dad home?; Stressed on the final syllable; drop the accent and papa means potato or pope depending on the country.
Three days ago; Día is masculine despite ending in -a so it takes los días; the greeting buenos días is always plural.
What does she say?; Decir he/she/usted present with the e to i change; dice que introduces reported speech and the que can never be dropped.
I need to talk to you; Necesitar yo present and fully regular; it takes a direct object with no preposition as in necesito dinero.
I didn't say that; Decir yo preterite; the irregular stem shifts the stress back so there is no accent unlike regular dí endings.
Hey have you got a minute?; The tú command of oír used as an attention-getter; oír is hearing while escuchar is deliberate listening.
I like this place; Gustar means to be pleasing so the thing liked is the subject and the person takes me or te; yo gusto is wrong.
I just wanted to see you; Querer imperfect for yo and él alike; it softens a request the way English uses I was hoping to.
Can it be true?; Ser he/she/usted future; Spanish also uses this future for guesses meaning it must be or it probably is.
There might be something; The infinitive behind hay and había; after another verb it carries the there is meaning as in debe haber.
Somewhere else; Feminine; en alguna parte means somewhere and formar parte de is to be part of something.
What's your name?; Masculine; in speech ¿cómo te llamas? is far more common and a nombre de means in the name of.
What a mess!; Literally shit and genuinely vulgar; used alone as a curse and after a noun as de mierda to mean lousy.
That must be true; Debe is deber for él/ella/usted and before an infinitive it means must or ought to; here it marks a guess about what is likely rather than an obligation.
I haven't seen anything; Visto is the irregular past participle of ver — never vido or veído — and it stays invariable after haber.
I don't care at all; Importar behaves like gustar: the thing that matters is the subject and the person goes in the me/te/le slot. No importa on its own means never mind.
They have a lot of money; Tienen is tener for ellos and for ustedes together; Latin Americans use it to address a group politely where Spain would say tenéis.
We've seen everything; Hemos is the we-form of haber and only ever an auxiliary — for possession Spanish uses tenemos.
You're right; Spanish says to have reason where English says to be right; razón is feminine and its plural razones loses the accent.
I want to know the truth; Saber is knowing facts or information while conocer is being acquainted with people and places.
Who did this?; Hizo is the irregular preterite of hacer for él/ella/usted; the z spelling appears only here while the yo form is hice.
Sometimes I don't know; Veces is the plural of vez with the z to c switch; a veces means sometimes and dos veces means twice.
They don't see anything; Ven is ver for ellos but it is also the tú command of venir meaning come here — only context separates them.
I have no idea; Idea is feminine and the stress falls on the e — i-de-a — so no accent is written; the clipped ni idea is the everyday way to say no clue.
There's a problem; Problema is masculine even though it ends in a — it comes from Greek — so el problema and los problemas.
What time is it?; Hora is feminine and means a clock hour or an appointment slot; time as an abstract quantity is tiempo.
Love of my life; Amor is masculine and mi amor is a normal endearment for a partner or a child; hacer el amor is the physical sense.
He doesn't see well; Ve is ver for él/ella/usted and simultaneously the tú command of ir — ve a casa means go home.
My whole family is here; Familia is feminine and grammatically singular so it takes a singular verb where British English often uses a plural.
The police are here; La policía is the force as a whole and takes a singular verb; un policía is a single male officer.
I should go; Debería is the conditional of deber and softens must into should; the yo and él forms are identical so a pronoun clears it up.
That girl doesn't like me; Chica is a girl or a young woman and is also the feminine adjective for small; in parts of Latin America it can mean girlfriend.
Let's go guys!; The masculine plural chicos covers a mixed group and is the usual way to address friends of any gender.
He tells me everything; Contar means both to tell a story and to count and its stem changes o to ue; the noun la cuenta is the bill.
What are you doing here?; Haces is hacer for tú covering both do and make; the simple present here translates as the English continuous.
I want to get out of here; Salir is leaving an enclosed place rather than departing on a trip; the yo form is irregular salgo and salir con means to date.
What a problem!; Vaya is the subjunctive of ir but as an exclamation it means wow or what a; it doubles as the usted command go.
See you tomorrow; Veo is the irregular yo form of ver; Spanish uses this plain present for a fixed future arrangement.
They're my friends; The masculine plural amigos includes women; amigo stays strictly platonic while novio is a romantic partner.
My brother is a police officer; Hermano is masculine and the plural hermanos means siblings of mixed gender.
I thought he was my friend; Pensé is the yo preterite of pensar and the written accent carries the stress; the e to ie change of pienso never happens in the preterite.
I didn't know anything about this; Sabía is the imperfect of saber shared by yo and él; supe would instead mean I found out at a moment.
I've got something in my head; Cabeza is feminine and beyond the body part it carries ideas — perder la cabeza is to lose one's head.
Thanks sweetheart; Cariño is a masculine noun meaning affection and stays masculine when used to address a woman; tener cariño a alguien is to be fond of someone.
What do I say now?; Digo is the irregular yo form of decir with an inserted g; dropped into a sentence it works as a filler meaning I mean.
Where are you all going?; Van is ir for ellos and for ustedes; with a plus an infinitive it becomes the everyday future they're going to.
Two men are here; Hombres is the plural of hombre; as a bare interjection hombre expresses surprise or protest rather than referring to a man.
We're friends; Somos is ser for nosotros and marks identity that defines us; estamos would describe a passing state or a location instead.
That's no way to talk; Forma is feminine and means both shape and manner; estar en forma is to be physically fit.
He's next to me; Lado is masculine and al lado de means beside; por otro lado shifts an argument to the other hand.
I have to talk to you; Debo is deber for yo and with an infinitive it means must; with a direct object like debo dinero it means I owe.
It would be a problem; Sería is the conditional of ser and yo and él share it; besides hypotheticals it politely softens a claim.
In that case I'm not going; Caso is masculine; hacer caso means to pay attention or obey and en caso de means in case of.
You can go out; Pueden is poder for ellos and ustedes with the o to ue change; it covers both being able and having permission.
What happened?; Pasó is the preterite of pasar for él; the accent is what separates it from paso; ¿qué pasa? asks about right now instead.
That boy is my brother; Chico is a boy or a young guy and as an adjective it means small — un coche chico.
I didn't do anything; Hice is the yo preterite of hacer and takes no written accent while the él form switches the c to a z in hizo.
There are a lot of people here; Personas is feminine even for a group of men and is what you count; gente is a singular mass noun and never takes a number.
Is the lady of the house in?; Señora is feminine and is used for a married or older woman while señorita marks a younger one; it also means wife.
I want to go back home; Volver is returning to where you came from and its present stem is vuelvo; volver a plus an infinitive means to do something again.
Let's go along that path; Camino is a masculine road or path and is also the yo form of caminar; en camino means on the way.
He's talking to my mother; Hablando is the gerund of hablar and only works after estar for an action in progress — as a subject Spanish needs the infinitive hablar.
No way; Manera is feminine and swaps freely with forma for way or method; de ninguna manera is a flat refusal.
Who is that person?; Persona is always feminine even for a man so una persona alta can be your brother.
I need your help; Feminine noun built from ayudar; shouted alone it is a cry for help while ¡Ayúdame! asks one specific person.
Do you know this story?; It covers both story and history so la historia de mi familia is a tale and not a school subject.
I was going to say something; Ir in the imperfect — yo and él share this form so only context says who; iba a plus infinitive is the past of voy a.
I suppose so; Suponer yo present with the irregular -go ending like tengo; speakers use it to hedge much as English drops in I guess.
I do not understand anything; Entender yo present with e turning into ie in the stem; entender is grasping meaning while comprender sounds formal.
Someone is at the door; Feminine; it stretches from a house door to a city gate to an airport gate while puerto with -o is a harbour.
Do you see what I mean?; Ver tú present — short and irregular; keep it apart from the noun vez which is a time or occasion.
Nothing is going to happen; Pasar spreads over to happen and to pass by and to spend time; pasar de something is to skip it.
What does that mean?; Significar third person singular; in everyday speech quiere decir is even more common for the same idea.
What day of the week is it?; Feminine; el fin de semana is the weekend and older speakers say ocho días for a week.
I hope to see you today; Esperar yo present does triple duty for hope and wait and expect; in the hope sense the next verb turns subjunctive.
One more year here; Masculine; the tilde is vital because ano without it is anus; hace un año means a year ago.
The kids are not here; The masculine plural covers mixed groups of boys and girls; these are small children while chicos suits teenagers.
Hey man! What are you doing?; Literally an uncle but in Spain it is the everyday word for dude; Latin Americans hear only the family sense.
You are so lucky!; Feminine; Spanish has luck rather than being lucky so it is tener suerte and ¡Suerte! alone wishes someone well.
We are going to another city; Feminine with the plural ciudades; a ciudad is a proper city while a small town is a pueblo.
He does not even know my name; It pairs with ni to mean not even and standing alone after a negative it sounds bookish.
Do you want to come with me?; Venir is motion toward the speaker so when someone calls you answer ya voy and never ya vengo.
My daughter is two years old; Feminine counterpart of hijo; the plural hijos covers children of both sexes together.
I would like to talk with you; Gustar in the conditional meaning it would please me so the thing desired is the subject and there is no yo form.
Wait five minutes; Masculine el minuto; un minuto by itself is just a moment rather than a measured length of time.
His father's death; Feminine despite the -e ending; muerto is the adjective and participle so you say está muerto and not está muerte.
Can you leave that here?; Dejar is leaving a thing behind or letting somebody do something; for leaving a place you need salir or irse.
Actually I do not know; Feminine; en realidad corrects what was just said instead of announcing anything about reality.
He does not stop talking; Dejar third person singular and also the tú command; dejar de plus infinitive is how Spanish says stop doing something.
We have problems; Masculine although it ends in -a because the root is Greek so it is los problemas and un problema grande.
Nobody gives me anything; Dar third person singular; the yo form is the odd doy and da igual means it makes no difference.
My heart is yours; Masculine and the plural corazones drops the accent; it also serves as an endearment like cariño.
I am scared; Masculine; fear is something you have in Spanish so it is tener miedo and never estar miedo.
Where is the boss?; Masculine with la jefa for a woman; it is a workplace supervisor and also a joking way to address a stranger.
I want a little water; Feminine yet it takes el agua because feminine nouns starting with stressed a- swap the article; adjectives stay feminine as in agua fría.
I have been waiting three hours; Plural of la hora; it serves for clock time and for stretches of time and ¿a qué hora? asks when.
Power is everything; This infinitive also works as a masculine noun so el poder is power while puedo is the verb.
My wife is at home; Feminine with esposo or marido for a husband; the plural esposas also means handcuffs.
Hands up!; Plural of la mano which stays feminine despite the -o so it is las manos frías.
You must see this; Deber tú present carrying obligation; tienes que sounds more forceful and deber de instead guesses that something is probably so.
Is anyone else coming?; Venir third person singular with the e to ie change; it points toward the speaker unlike va.
Come on! Let's go!; The subjunctive of venir doubling as the usted command; in Spain a bare ¡Venga! means fine or come on.
She has her mother's eyes; Masculine plural of el ojo; body parts take the article and not a possessive and ¡Ojo! warns you to watch out.
I want to find a place; The o becomes ue when stressed as in encuentro; encontrarse con somebody is bumping into them by chance.
Give me your hand; Feminine although it ends in -o so la mano and mi mano derecha; the diminutive manita is common.
That boy is my son; A niño is a small child while chico reaches up to young men; de niño means when I was a kid.
I do not want to see your face; Feminine; tener buena cara is looking healthy and the adjective caro instead means expensive.
Careful with the water!; A masculine noun for care; tener cuidado is how you say be careful and con names the danger.
Three nights without you; Plural of la noche; buenas noches both greets and says goodbye and de noche means at night.
It is the end of the world; Masculine; por fin is at last and fin de semana is the weekend while final points to a last scene or match.
Shall we go for a drink?; Tomar takes something and also drinks it so tomar algo is having a drink; in Spain coger grabs but tomar consumes.
Listen to your mother; Escuchar third person and tú command; escuchar is deliberate listening while oír is just hearing a sound.
We are about to leave; Masculine; a punto de plus infinitive is about to and un punto is also a dot or a full stop.
Is he still here?; Sigue is seguir third person present and also the tú command; with a place or adjective it means still is rather than follows.
I hope there is water; Haya is the present subjunctive twin of hay; espero que forces it and hay would be wrong after que.
My team is my family; Equipo is masculine and also means the gear or kit for a job; it never means the match itself.
Your father needs help; Necesita is necesitar third person so it serves él ella and usted; with a friend you say necesitas.
What time are you going to arrive?; Llegar takes a before a place never en; venir instead means coming toward the speaker.
The doctor is already here; Doctor works as a title of address on its own and drops the article when you call the person; the feminine is doctora.
If only there were time; Hubiera is the past subjunctive of haber for unreal wishes and if-clauses; after ojalá it signals the thing is not so.
My car is at home; Coche is the everyday word in Spain while most of Latin America says carro or auto.
What do I do now?; Hago is the irregular yo form of hacer and the g shows up only there since the rest runs haces hace hacemos.
I have class in the morning; Clase is feminine and also means kind or sort; tener clase takes no article.
Why do you say that?; Dices is decir tú present; the stem vowel turns to i in digo dices dice but stays e in decimos.
What is your mother's name?; Llamarse is literally how she calls herself which is how Spanish asks names; without se llama means calls or phones.
Take my hand; Toma as a command is what you say while handing something over like here you go; tomar also covers drinking.
The earth is our home; Tierra is feminine and stretches over soil land and the planet; the planet gets a capital in writing.
This war has no end; Guerra is feminine; dar guerra is the idiom for being a handful.
Let me think for a moment; Pensar en is to think about something pensar de is your opinion of it and pensar plus infinitive means to intend.
I hope she can come; Pueda is the subjunctive of poder where o becomes ue; espero que requires this mood.
There is blood in the water; Sangre is feminine and has no ordinary plural; a sangre fría means in cold blood.
The women are here already; Mujeres is the plural of mujer with the stress still on the last syllable; mujer also means wife.
Just one more lap; Vuelta is a turn a lap or the change you get back; dar la vuelta is to turn around.
It was me; Fui is the preterite yo form shared by ser and ir so only context tells them apart; here it is ser.
I don't want to work today; Trabajar en names the workplace and trabajar de names the job you do.
I haven't had time; Tenido is the participle of tener and appears with haber where it never changes for gender.
I like this game; Juego is masculine and is spelled the same as the yo form of jugar so watch the context.
His body isn't well; Cuerpo is masculine and also means a corps or body of people; de cuerpo entero means full-length.
Can I come in?; Entrar takes en in Spain and a in much of Latin America but never a bare object.
Nobody believes me; Creer a a person is believing what they say while creer en is believing in something or someone.
She couldn't speak; Podía is the imperfect and paints an ongoing inability whereas pudo would mean she failed at one moment.
We have to go now; Debemos is deber nosotros present; deber plus infinitive is obligation while deber de plus infinitive is a guess.
Give me a chance; Oportunidad is feminine and is the normal word for a chance; luck is suerte instead.
Where is my phone?; Teléfono keeps its accent on the second e; on the phone is por teléfono.
We need more time; Necesitamos is the nosotros present; necesitar takes its object directly and necesitar de sounds bookish.
In the end nothing happened; El final is an ending while la final is a championship match; al final means in the end.
Are you going to the party?; Fiesta is feminine and also means a public holiday; you hacer una fiesta rather than make one.
Where were you last night?; Estabas is the imperfect tú form of estar and is normal for past location while estuviste sounds like a finished visit.
Everybody wants money; Quieren covers ellos and ustedes; querer a a person shifts the meaning to loving them.
My brother's car; Auto is short for automóvil and is usual in Mexico and the Southern Cone where Spain says coche.
Can you give me something?; Dar is badly irregular with doy and di and it builds idioms like dar miedo to be scary.
I want to live here; Vivir en is where you live and vivir de is what you live on; it also just means to be alive.
My sister knows nothing; Hermana is feminine while the plural hermanos covers a mixed set of siblings.
What's your number?; Número is masculine and keeps its accent; ask with cuál not qué when choosing among known things.
Just two more months; Meses adds es because mes ends in a consonant and the stress stays put so no accent is written.
It's not my fault; Culpa is feminine; tener la culpa is to be at fault and echar la culpa is to blame someone.
The kids are at school; Escuela is feminine and usually means primary school while colegio and instituto cover later years.
He has already left; Ido is the participle of ir but with se the verb means to leave rather than to go.
What are you saying?; Diciendo is the gerund of decir with the stem vowel switched to i; estar plus gerund is the only way to build the progressive.
Your boss talks a lot; Habla is hablar third person and the tú command; hablar con is to talk to someone and hablar de is about a topic.
Maybe it's in the car; Esté is the subjunctive of estar with a written accent; quizás pulls the subjunctive when you are unsure.
I have a question; Pregunta is the noun and preguntar the verb; you hacer una pregunta since decir never works here.
The girls are talking; Chicas covers girls and young women and the masculine chicos is what you use for a mixed group.
Were they your friends?; Imperfect of ser for they or ustedes — it describes how people and things used to be; a single finished past event would use fueron instead.
What's going on?; Gerund of pasar; with estar it reports something unfolding right now. Pasar also means to pass by or to spend time.
Where is the captain?; Masculine noun for the military rank and for a team captain; the plural capitanes loses the written accent.
My sister has a baby; Bebé stays masculine even for a girl unless you deliberately say la bebé; the accent puts the stress on the last syllable and the plural is bebés.
We don't know anything; Saber we-form present; the irregularity of this verb sits only in yo sé so sabemos is regular. It is knowledge of facts rather than of people.
Do you like the food?; Feminine noun that means food in general and also the main meal of the day — in Spain that is lunch rather than dinner.
I don't want to die; Infinitive of morir; the o becomes ue when stressed as in muero. Adding the pronoun as morirse softens it or makes it figurative like dying of laughter.
I don't know that man; Conocer yo present with the irregular -zc- spelling; conocer is being acquainted with people or places while saber is knowing facts. A person needs the personal a in front.
Shall we go eat something?; Infinitive to eat; ir a plus an infinitive is the everyday way to talk about the near future. On its own comer often means to have lunch.
A wine please; Masculine el vino; the same spelling is also the preterite of venir so only context tells you which one you are hearing.
Do you have the list?; Feminine noun for a list; it doubles as the adjective meaning ready with estar and clever with ser.
I want him to do it; Present subjunctive of hacer for él ella or usted and also the polite usted command; querer que always forces this mood.
I have two children; The masculine plural covers sons and any mixed group of sons and daughters; only an all-girl group uses hijas.
My parents are here; In the plural padre normally means the two parents together rather than several fathers; that other reading needs clear context.
The room is ready; Feminine like every -ción noun; it points to a bedroom or hotel room while cuarto is vaguer. The plural drops the accent as habitaciones.
I can't believe this; Infinitive to believe; creer que takes the indicative but the negative no creo que takes the subjunctive. Creer en is to believe in something.
I'm thinking about you; Gerund of pensar; pensar en is to have someone on your mind while pensar de asks for an opinion. The e to ie change vanishes outside the stressed forms.
It was two days; Preterite they-form of both ser and ir — one form for two verbs. It states a finished fact whereas eran paints ongoing background.
What's it about?; Tratarse de is the set phrase for what something is about; tratar de plus infinitive means to try and tratar a alguien is to treat a person.
I'm looking for you; Gerund of buscar; the verb takes no preposition at all so never say busco por. Only a human object adds the personal a.
I was never afraid; Preterite yo of tener with the irregular stem tuv- and an unstressed ending. Tenía would instead describe a lasting state.
I love you so much; Amar yo present; it is weightier than te quiero which is what couples and families actually say daily. As a noun el amo means master.
You're very young; The same form serves both genders as el joven and la joven; the plural jóvenes picks up an accent. Used alone it names a young person.
A couple of hours; Masculine noun; un par de is the normal way to say a couple of. The unrelated phrase a la par means at the same rate.
What are they doing here?; Hacer for they or ustedes; the only irregular present form is yo hago. Here it asks what people are up to rather than what they make.
We'll keep going like this; Infinitive meaning to continue or to follow; the e turns into i as in sigo. Seguir plus a gerund is how Spanish says to keep on doing something.
What do they say?; Decir for they or ustedes with the e to i change on top of the irregular yo digo. Dicen que is the standard opener for reported gossip.
I haven't got a clue; Literally a whore but far more often a vulgar intensifier; this phrase is very crude so keep it away from strangers and work.
They don't know anything; Saber for they or ustedes; the form itself is regular even though yo is the odd sé. It covers facts and information not acquaintance with people.
It doesn't make sense; Masculine noun for meaning sense and also direction of travel; it is identical to the past participle of sentir.
Don't do that; Negative tú command of hacer; negative commands borrow the subjunctive so no haces is wrong. The affirmative command is the short haz.
We have to wait a bit; One infinitive does the work of to wait to hope and to expect; when you wait for a person add a as in esperar a mi hermana.
He has a weapon; The noun is feminine yet takes el arma because it starts with a stressed a; in the plural it goes back to las armas.
That's five dollars; The accent on dólar survives in the plural dólares; Spanish writes currency names in lowercase.
They were at the house; Estar imperfect for they or ustedes; it sets the scene or a lasting position in the past. Eran would give identity rather than place.
It's for your safety; Feminine as all -dad nouns are; it covers safety and security and also confidence — con seguridad means surely.
He was here yesterday; Preterite of estar for él ella or usted built on the irregular stem estuv-; it frames a finished stay while estaba would be background.
Don't worry; A subjunctive doing duty as the negative tú command of preocuparse; the te is obligatory and the polite version is no se preocupe.
Give me your word; Feminine noun for a word and for a promise you make; a swearword is a palabrota.
We're waiting for you; Gerund of esperar; paired with estar it means waiting at this moment. Nothing like for goes before the thing awaited.
There's nothing left; Quedar for what remains; with a pronoun quedarse means to stay and quedar con alguien is to arrange to meet someone.
Is he in his office?; Feminine noun for a workplace office or a public bureau; a doctor's room is a consulta instead.
You can't kill anyone; Regular infinitive to kill; the personal a is needed before the victim. Matarse covers dying in an accident and also working yourself to death.
I'll go with you; Future yo of ir formed on ir plus é so the accent is essential; in speech voy a ir is much more common than this tense.
The baby is in bed; Feminine noun; hacer la cama is to make the bed and irse a la cama is to turn in for the night.

I haven't heard anything; Participle of oír and the i needs its accent to break the vowels apart; the same word is the noun for the inner ear. Oír is passive hearing while escuchar is deliberate listening.
There wouldn't be any problems; Conditional of haber; standing alone it means there would be and before a participle it builds would have. It is not interchangeable with the subjunctive hubiera.
Where can my phone be?; Estar future for él ella or usted; Spanish very often uses this future to guess about the present so it reads as I wonder where it is.
He gave me his number; Preterite of dar for él ella or usted; dar is so short that di and dio carry no written accent at all.
It's a keepsake from my father; Masculine noun for a memory or a souvenir; it is spelled exactly like recuerdo meaning I remember. In the plural recuerdos also sends regards.
He is not being fair; The gerund of ser is rare because ser describes what things are; estar siendo frames identity as temporary behaviour someone is choosing right now.
I hope he is right; Subjunctive third person of tener after espero que; it is also the polite command form for usted so ¡tenga! means here you are.
There is no light here; Feminine despite ending in z and its plural is luces; it covers daylight; a lamp and the electricity supply.
What the hell is he doing?; Plural demonio used as a mild swear filler after qué; singular el demonio is the actual devil and would not fit here.
I want to sleep a bit; Dormir is being asleep while dormirse is falling asleep; it stem-changes to duermo in the present.
This is not his place; Masculine and means spot or seat rather than lugar's wider sense of place; un sitio web is a website.
Can I help with something?; Ayudar takes a personal a before the person helped as in ayudar a mi madre; the thing you help with follows con or en.
I have to get hold of some money; Conseguir is obtaining after effort unlike neutral tener or recibir; the e becomes i in consigo.
My husband knows nothing; Masculine and the everyday word for husband; esposo sounds more formal and mujer is often used for wife where English keeps husband and wife parallel.
Leave me alone; Feminine noun paz means peace and its plural is paces; en paz here is idiomatic for alone rather than peaceful.
I do not like your plan; Masculine and its plural is planes with an added e; tener plan de is not used - Spanish says planear or pensar plus infinitive.
He has given me his word; Regular past participle of dar; with haber it never agrees so it stays dado even about a woman.
His father died yesterday; Third person preterite of morir with a stem vowel change to u; morirse adds an emotional or sudden sense as in se murió de repente.
The whole village knows; Masculine and means both a small town and a people as a nation; the sense comes from context alone.
Has anyone come?; Participle of venir; venir is coming toward the speaker so a Spanish speaker says voy where English says I am coming to you.
Enough problems already!; Bastar is used impersonally in the third person; basta con eso means that is enough and it never takes a personal subject like I.
One step at a time; Masculine noun for a step or pace; identical in spelling to paso from pasar so only the article tells you it is a noun.
We should talk about this; Conditional of deber for we and it is the polite way to suggest; debemos hablar would sound like a hard obligation.
I like this music; Feminine and used without an article after de as in clase de música; it also covers sheet music and a band's sound.
I want him to tell the truth; Present subjunctive of decir built on the digo stem; as an usted command diga is how you answer the phone - ¿diga?.
Hold on a minute; Masculine and in speech it rarely means sixty seconds; it is the general just a second the way English uses minute.
I am going to call the police; Llamar covers phoning; shouting for; and naming; llamarse is what you use for your own name.
Nobody thinks about me; Third person of pensar with the e to ie change; pensar en is having something on your mind while pensar que states an opinion.
It is not my country; Masculine and the accent stays in both numbers — país and países — because the i is pronounced separately.
I am the king of the world; Masculine with plural reyes; los Reyes can mean the king and queen together or the Three Wise Men at Epiphany.
Sorry about yesterday; Masculine noun used as a standalone apology or to get past someone; perdona and perdone are the verb forms if you want to say excuse me to a person.
More time is needed; Feminine noun for a lack; hacer falta is the normal way to say something is needed and the thing needed is the subject not the object.
I think about you always; First person of pensar; the yo form keeps the ie change while pensamos loses it.
Where the hell were you?; Plural diablo works exactly like demonios as an intensifier after a question word; it is mild and common in dubbing.
I have lost my job; Participle of perder; perder covers losing objects; missing a train and losing a game so context decides the English.
That girl is my daughter; Feminine niña is a child up to about twelve while chica starts around the teens; calling a grown woman niña sounds patronising.
Are you all right miss?; Feminine title once meaning unmarried and now dated; señora is the safer address for any adult woman you do not know.
He has been waiting two hours; Llevar plus a time span plus a gerund is the standard way to say how long something has been going on where English uses have been.
He is in hospital; Masculine and Spanish keeps the article el where British English drops it; the plural hospitales adds es.
Somebody has called you; Participle of llamar; with ser it means named as in un hombre llamado Juan; here with haber it is the phone call sense.
What do we do now?; First person plural present of hacer and identical to the command let us do; only tone and context separate the two.
Can you take me home?; Llevar is carrying something away from here while traer is bringing it toward the speaker.
Got a light?; Masculine and literally fire; asking for fuego is the normal way to ask for a light for a cigarette.
It was his fault; Third person preterite of tener and irregular with no accent on the o; tener la culpa is the set phrase for being to blame.
I am going to put some music on; Poner is placing or switching on and its yo form is pongo; ponerse plus clothing is putting it on yourself.
There are people in the street; Feminine despite ending in e; en la calle also means outdoors or homeless depending on context.
He has just left; Acabar de plus infinitive is the only natural way to say has just done something; on its own acabar means to finish.
It is the proof I need; Feminine and stretches from proof to a test to a rehearsal or a fitting; a school exam is usually examen.
This book is mine; Masculine; note libro is the physical book while libre with an e means free so the two are unrelated.
Everything is in order; Masculine el orden is arrangement or sequence but feminine la orden is a command or a religious order; the article changes the meaning.
He was here for two weeks; Plural of semana; Spanish needs no preposition for a duration so no word matches the English for.
Do you want a coffee?; Masculine and the accent falls on the last syllable; the plural is cafés and the same word names the cafe you drink it in.
We are going to start now; Empezar and comenzar are interchangeable; empezar a plus infinitive is the pattern and the yo form is empiezo.
We want to talk with you; First person plural of querer and one of the forms that keeps the plain e; queremos also means we love when a person follows.
Whose dog is this?; Masculine with perra as the female; perra used of a woman is a strong insult so stick to the masculine as the general word.
Look at the sky; Masculine noun for both sky and heaven — el cielo covers the religious sense too and cielo is also a pet name like sweetheart.
What is your position?; Masculine noun meaning post or job position; it also means a market stall and it is the past participle of poner so context decides.
How was the trip?; Masculine noun despite the -e ending; it is the journey itself while a holiday abroad is unas vacaciones.
What would he do?; Hacer in the conditional for él/ella/usted — the same form serves I would do so add yo if it is unclear who acts.
Do not ask any more questions; Feminine plural of pregunta; Spanish says hacer una pregunta not decir so the verb is hacer.
What do you think?; Pensar you-singular present with the e-to-ie stem change; pensar en means to think about something and pensar plus infinitive means to plan to.
I have always loved you; Past participle of querer; as an adjective it means dear and it opens letters as querido Juan.
I am going to get help; Infinitive covering both to look for and to fetch — no preposition follows it so busco a mi hermano needs no for.
I will not tell you anything; Decir in the future for yo and one of the irregular futures built on dir- not decir-.
That sounds good; Sonar he/she/it present with the o-to-ue change; do not confuse it with soñar which is to dream.
Do you want to play with me?; Jugar is playing a game while tocar is playing an instrument; it takes a in jugar al fútbol.
I need change for the coffee; Masculine noun for change as in coins or a switch; en cambio as a phrase means on the other hand.
Let us watch a movie; Feminine noun that also means a roll of film; the cinema building is el cine.
That is worth millions; Plural of millón and it keeps de before a noun as in dos millones de personas.
There will be a party tomorrow; The future of impersonal hay; it stays singular even with plural things as in habrá muchos problemas.
The rest is for you; Masculine noun for the remainder; the plural los restos means remains or leftovers.
See you tomorrow; Ver we-present; the reflexive nos vemos is the standard casual goodbye rather than a statement about seeing.
The president is speaking now; Masculine but the same form serves a woman as la presidente although la presidenta is common.
Where are my clothes?; Feminine and always singular in Spanish even though English uses a plural; one garment is una prenda.
I do not want to waste time; Perder covers losing and missing a train and wasting time; the yo form is irregular pierdo.
Come back home now; Volver he/she/it present and also the tú command; volver a plus infinitive means to do something again.
The agent wants to talk to you; Noun with one form for both genders — la agente for a woman with only the article changing.
I have no words; Feminine plural of palabra; tomar la palabra is to take the floor and a swear word is una palabrota.
There is no information yet; Feminine and uncountable so never informaciones for pieces of information.
What will he do now?; Hacer future for él/ella/usted with the shortened har- stem.
Do you understand what I am saying?; Entender you-singular present; it is the everyday verb for grasping meaning while comprender sounds more formal.
I am working here; Gerund of trabajar; Spanish uses the simple present for habits so use trabajo aquí for your usual job.
I was just trying to help; Gerund of tratar and it needs de before an infinitive; tratarse de means to be about something.
It is a fair deal; Masculine noun for a deal or agreement and also how you treat someone; ¡trato hecho! seals a bargain.
Can I use your phone?; Usar is the plain to use while utilizar is its more formal twin; for wearing clothes Spanish also says usar.
You have no right; Masculine noun for a legal right and also the field of law; as an adjective it means right-hand or straight.
No way; Masculine noun for manner; de modo que means so that and modo is interchangeable with manera in most phrases.
Call me whenever you like; Querer subjunctive for tú — cuando plus subjunctive is required for a future moment that has not happened.
We could go tomorrow; Poder conditional for nosotros on the irregular podr- stem; it is the polite way to float a suggestion.
Have you seen the news?; Feminine plural; one item is una noticia so a single piece of news is grammatically singular here.
I have not found it; Past participle of encontrar; encontrarse con someone is to run into them and encontrarse also describes how you feel.
Everything is under control; Masculine noun and also a checkpoint or an inspection; the plural is controles.
There is no room for hate; Masculine noun for hatred but also the yo form of odiar so yo odio means I hate.
I am in front of your house; Frente a means facing or opposite; el frente is a war front while la frente is your forehead.
Sex is not love; Masculine noun covering both the act and the male or female category as in sexo masculino.
I will be here tomorrow; Estar future for yo and the accent on the final syllable is what marks the future — estare without it is not a word.
They have guns!; Plural of arma which is feminine yet takes el arma in the singular because of the stressed a sound.
Do you remember my name?; Recordar you-singular present with the o-to-ue change; it takes no preposition so never recordar de.
She is a friend of my sister; Feminine of amigo; using mi amiga about a girlfriend can imply romance so people say una amiga to stay neutral.
The group is already here; Masculine and it takes a singular verb even though it names many people.
It is none of your business; Masculine noun for a matter or affair; asuntos exteriores is foreign affairs.
I have just arrived; Acabar yo present and acabar de plus infinitive is the normal way to say you just did something.
Leave a message; Masculine noun despite ending in -e; a text is un mensaje de texto and mandar is the usual verb for sending one.
Thank you for your attention; Feminine noun; prestar atención is to pay attention and ¡atención! works as a shouted warning.
That hurts; Masculine noun for harm; hacer daño is the normal way to say to hurt and hacerse daño is to hurt yourself.
What's going on here?; Suceder is happen; it is the neutral written-sounding verb where speech usually says pasar — ¿qué pasa? is far more common out loud.
I don't want to change anything; Cambiar covers both changing something and changing yourself; for changing clothes or trains Spanish adds a reflexive or de — cambiarse; cambiar de tren.
Don't be like that; Seas is the ser subjunctive for tú and it is the form negative commands must use; there is no negative form built on eres.
What have you got in your mouth?; La boca is feminine; it also means the mouth of a river or a tunnel; the shut-up command is cállate la boca — never a literal close-your-mouth.
She left me yesterday; Dejó is dejar third-person preterite and covers left as in abandoned and left behind an object; for leaving a place yourself you need salir or irse.
It was my mistake; El error is masculine and everyday Spanish for a mistake; cometer un error is the verb pairing — never hacer un error.
Along the way; Largo is length as a noun even though you meet it far more as the adjective long; a lo largo de is a fixed phrase meaning along or throughout.
It's worth it; La pena is grief or pity; valer la pena is the idiom for being worth the trouble and qué pena on its own means what a shame.
Listen to her voice; La voz is feminine and its plural is las voces; en voz alta means aloud rather than in a loud voice.
I don't think about the future; El futuro is the noun; as a time expression Spanish says en el futuro where English drops the article in phrases like in future.
My mother doesn't feel well; Siente is sentir for él or ella; reflexive sentirse describes how someone feels while plain sentir takes an object — siento frío.
It's a secret between us; El secreto works as noun and adjective; en secreto means secretly and guardar un secreto is the verb you keep it with.
Where's the bathroom?; El baño is the room and also a bath; in Latin America you also hear el servicio or el sanitario and asking for it with dónde está is the polite default.
I thought he was your friend; Pensaba is the imperfect and serves both yo and él; it reports a belief you held over time whereas pensé marks the moment the thought struck.
She's my girlfriend; La novia is a girlfriend and also a bride at a wedding; the masculine novio works the same way so context tells you which.
I'm sleepy now; El sueño is both a dream and sleepiness; tener sueño is being sleepy while estar soñando is dreaming.
Do whatever you want; Haz is the irregular tú command from hacer and drops the expected e; the usted form is haga and the negative is no hagas.
I've got no strength today; La fuerza is strength or force; the plural las fuerzas often means armed forces and a la fuerza means by force or unwillingly.
They have to wait here; Deben is deber for ellos and expresses obligation; add de and it flips to probability — deben de estar aquí means they must be here.
What am I supposed to do?; Suponer means to suppose or assume; the impersonal se supone que is the standard way Spanish says supposed to.
We were at the party; Estábamos is the estar imperfect for nosotros and sets a background scene; estuvimos would frame the whole visit as finished.
I was there for two hours; Estuve is the estar preterite for yo and bounds the stay; estaba would leave the duration open.
I didn't find my phone; Encontré is encontrar preterite for yo and keeps the o of the stem because the stress moves to the ending.
He's come back home; Vuelto is the irregular past participle of volver; volver a plus an infinitive means to do something again.
I'm in a lot of pain; El dolor is pain and takes de for the body part — dolor de cabeza; Spanish says tener dolor or duele rather than a verb for hurt.
I love your house; Encantar works backwards like gustar so the thing loved is the subject and me is the one delighted; for people Spanish uses querer or amar instead.
How old are you?; La edad is age and Spanish asks with tener not ser; the shorter cuántos años tienes is more common in speech.
He's standing over there; El pie is the foot and its plural is los pies; estar de pie means standing and a pie means on foot.
I want to earn money; Ganar covers both earning and winning; ganar a alguien is beating a person while ganarse la vida is making a living.
There's no air in here; El aire is masculine; it also means a draught and al aire libre means outdoors.
I'm very sorry; Lamento is lamentar for yo and is a formal apology or condolence; lo siento is the everyday version and the noun lamento means a moan.
It was a murder; El asesinato is the act while el asesino is the killer; Spanish keeps the two words apart where English reuses murder.
Nobody saw me go in; Vio is ver preterite for él and carries no accent unlike vi and vieron patterns; after verbs of perception Spanish uses a plain infinitive where English uses -ing.
The moment has come; Llegado is llegar's participle; llegar means to arrive somewhere and needs a for the destination — llegar a casa.
Excuse me can you help me?; Disculpe is the usted command from disculpar and is how you flag down a stranger politely; disculpa is the tú version and perdón works for both.
I have an appointment tomorrow; La cita is an appointment of any kind including with a doctor and only sometimes a romantic date; it also means a quotation.
Without you I wouldn't be here; Estaría is the estar conditional for yo and él alike; it states what would be the case and pairs with si clauses.
Why did you go there?; Fuiste is the preterite tú form of ir but the identical form also belongs to ser; only context tells you whether it means you went or you were.
I don't understand this system; Sistema ends in a yet is masculine like problema and tema because of its Greek origin — el sistema.
Pleased to meet you madam; El gusto is taste or pleasure; mucho gusto is the fixed greeting on being introduced and el gusto es mío is the reply.
I run a business here; El negocio is a business or a deal; los negocios means business in general as in hombre de negocios.
That's in your head; La mente is feminine and means the mind as faculty; for memory Spanish prefers memoria and tener en mente means to bear in mind.
To live in the countryside; El campo is the countryside and also a field or a sports pitch; en el campo contrasts with en la ciudad.
Take a look at this; Mire is the usted command from mirar and the tú version is mira; mirar is looking on purpose while ver is just seeing.
You don't understand the situation; La situación is feminine and its plural drops the accent — situaciones; it also means the location of a building.
We're at the hotel; El hotel is masculine and stressed on the last syllable; the h is silent so it sounds like o-tel.
This doesn't work; Funcionar is used for machines and plans working; for a person working you need trabajar.
I want a photo with you; La foto is feminine because it shortens la fotografía even though it ends in o; the plural is las fotos.
I need a lawyer now; El abogado is a lawyer and the feminine is la abogada; abogar por means to advocate for something.
I've finished my work; Terminado is terminar's participle; terminar and acabar are interchangeable for finishing but acabar de plus infinitive means to have just done something.
I have to pay for the hotel; Infinitive of pagar; the thing bought takes por as in pagar por la comida but the bill or the price itself is a plain direct object.
He killed my father; Third-person preterite of matar; a human object needs the personal a even though English has no equivalent.
I'll call you tomorrow; Llamar means both to call by phone and to name; with a reflexive pronoun it becomes me llamo for stating your own name.
How do you feel today?; Reflexive sentirse is how you feel; drop the te and sentir means to feel something or to regret it.
What's wrong with you?; Ocurrir is used impersonally for things happening to someone; it also covers an idea occurring to you as in se me ocurre algo.
Nobody remembers my name; Recordar is stem-changing o to ue in the present; it also means to remind someone and takes no reflexive pronoun unlike acordarse de.
It's half the money; Feminine noun; Spanish says la mitad de rather than using half as an adjective before the noun.
Do whatever she wants; Present subjunctive of querer; after lo que it signals an open unknown choice where the indicative quiere would name one specific wish.
I like your hair; Masculine and singular for a whole head of hair; cabello is the polite alternative and un pelo is a single strand.
Were you scared?; Tener you-singular imperfect for how things were over a stretch of past time; tuviste miedo would point at one single moment of fear.
Did you see my photo?; Ver you-singular preterite; it is spelled the same as a form of vestir so context decides and it carries no accent.
My sister arrived late; Third-person preterite of llegar; the accent carries the stress and llego without it means I arrive.
Thanks for your company; Feminine noun covering both a business firm and the company of another person; the accent on the í splits it from the a so the word has four syllables.
We have no relationship at all; Feminine like all nouns in -ción and the plural adds -es while dropping the accent as relaciones.
My father knows the city; Conocer is being familiar with places and people while saber is knowing facts; the first person is irregular as conozco.
I don't want anything to happen; Present subjunctive of pasar required after quiero que; on its own ¡pase! is the polite invitation to come in.
I have loads of work; Masculine; literally a heap and colloquially un montón de works like English tons of.
I thought he was my friend; Creer first-person preterite with the accent on the í; creí is a belief you have since dropped while creía describes a lasting assumption.
Dinner is ready; Feminine noun for the evening meal; the verb cenar means to eat it so no extra word like have is needed.
I can't feel my hand; Infinitive; lo siento uses this same verb to apologise so sentir covers physical sensation and regret alike.
It was through my brother; Almost always in the fixed phrase a través de meaning across or by way of; it is never used as a noun on its own.
It was an accident; Masculine despite the -e ending; it means a car crash as well as a mishap and the word itself blames nobody.
You were the boss; Ser you-singular imperfect for describing a past role or state; fuiste would frame it as one finished event.
He couldn't help; Poder third-person preterite meaning he tried and failed at that moment; podía would only describe a lasting inability.
My mother lives here; Vivir third-person present and fully regular; it also means to be alive so vive can answer whether someone survived.
See you around; Feminine noun for sight or a view; this is a set farewell and punto de vista is a point of view.
Hold the line; Feminine with the accent on the í; it covers a phone line a queue and a drawn line alike.
This way gentlemen; Plural of caballero which originally meant a horseman; it is the polite address for men and the label on men's toilets.
What will we do now?; Hacer we-form future; the stem is the irregular har- rather than hacer- while the ending is the standard future one.
They really scare me; Dar third-person plural present; dar miedo is the normal way to say something frightens you with the frightened person as an indirect object.
I'm going to the shop; Feminine; it also means a tent as in tienda de campaña.
I want to buy a car; Regular infinitive; the person you buy from also takes a so comprar a alguien can mean buying from or for them.
Have you understood the question?; Past participle of entender and invariable after haber; entendido on its own works as an acknowledgement like understood.
I work downtown; Masculine; el centro means the city centre or downtown with no extra word needed.
That was a month ago; Masculine and the plural is meses; hace plus a time span is how Spanish says ago.
It's very sunny today; Masculine; Spanish treats sunshine as a quantity you have so hace sol or hay sol replaces an adjective.
Don't be silly; Works as noun and adjective and becomes tonta for a woman; it is teasing between friends but insulting from a stranger.
I'm really hungry; Feminine despite el hambre which takes el only to avoid the clash of two a sounds so you still say mucha; tener hambre literally has hunger.
The food is on the table; Feminine; poner la mesa is to set the table and a flat-topped hill is also a mesa.
I need an answer now; Feminine; it covers an answer or a reaction and the verb is responder or contestar.
It's a letter from my daughter; Feminine; the same word is a playing card and a restaurant menu as in a la carta.
We have no evidence; Plural of prueba; in the plural it usually means evidence or proof while the singular is a test or an attempt.
That's her boyfriend; Masculine; the same word means groom at a wedding and novia is the feminine pair.
Do you like my eyes?; Gustar agrees with the thing liked and not the liker so a plural thing forces gustan while the person stays an indirect object.
I couldn't sleep last night; Poder first-person preterite; the stem vowel becomes u and the ending takes no accent unlike regular -í preterites.
Whose suit is this?; Masculine despite the -e ending; it means a suit or an outfit and traje is also the preterite of traer so context matters.
Give me the address; Feminine; it means a postal address a direction of travel and the management of a company.
They told me the truth; Decir third-person plural preterite built on the irregular dij- stem with no accent on the ending.
It's been a pleasure; Masculine; con placer is a warm yes to a request and placer as a verb survives only in very formal writing.
I hope they'll be friends; Ser third-person plural present subjunctive triggered by espero que; the indicative son would state it as plain fact.
He will have to wait; Future of tener third person singular; tener que plus infinitive is the everyday way to say have to; this same form covers él ella and usted.
Where is the boat?; Masculine el barco covers anything from a rowboat to a ship; a big passenger ship is often un buque or un crucero.
My teacher is very young; Masculine; the feminine is la profesora and the plural los profesores keeps no accent shift; Spanish uses profesor for school teachers too not only at university.
Thanks for the service; Masculine; in a restaurant el servicio can also mean the tip included and in Spain los servicios are the toilets.
That boy is my son; Masculine and quite dated or regional; chico is the neutral everyday word and in Mexico chavo or in Argentina pibe is what you actually hear.
I have a meeting at three; Feminine; note the accent on the last syllable which disappears in the plural reuniones; it means a meeting or gathering not a reunion of old friends.
I have left it at home; Past participle of dejar; participles after haber never change for gender so it stays dejado even if a woman says it.
That is the law; Feminine despite ending in a consonant and the plural is leyes; la ley is law as rules while el derecho is law as a field of study.
I would like to speak with you; Past subjunctive of querer used as a polite request; softer than quiero and more formal than me gustaría.
There was an accident; The past of hay from haber; use hubo for a single completed event and había for background description.
I like this show; Masculine even though it ends in a because it comes from Greek like problema and tema; the plural is los programas.
My career is over; Feminine; carrera also means a race or a university degree so estudio una carrera means I am doing a degree.
Today is my birthday; Masculine and already ends in s so it never changes in the plural; you say feliz cumpleaños never buen cumpleaños.
Let us go guys!; Plural of muchacho and used to address a mixed group; chicos is the modern neutral choice and Spain prefers chicos or tíos.
A pain in the ass; Masculine and crude everywhere though in Spain it lands milder than the English word; trasero is the polite choice.
I love this song; Feminine; the accent goes when it becomes canciones; a canción is the song itself while la letra is the lyrics.
My daughter is at university; Feminine; Spanish says en la universidad with the article where English drops it.
Are you going to the wedding?; Feminine and it is the ceremony and party; el matrimonio is the marriage as an institution and casarse is to get married.
Do not be afraid; This is tener you-singular subjunctive which is exactly what a negative command needs; the affirmative would be ten miedo.
What did your father do?; Imperfect of hacer for repeated or ongoing past; hizo would ask about one finished action instead.
I hope you are well; Estar you-singular subjunctive triggered by espero que; the indicative estás would be wrong after that verb.
I will wait for you in the living room; Feminine; la sala is a living room in Latin America while Spain says el salón and a hospital ward is also una sala.
I have been here two hours; First person of llevar; llevar plus a time span is how Spanish expresses how long something has been going on with no perfect tense.
It is your decision; Feminine and the plural is decisiones; you take a decision with tomar not with hacer.
Wait a moment please; Subjunctive of esperar working as the usted command; to a friend you would say espera.
Pass me the salt; Feminine la sal even though it looks masculine; do not confuse it with sal the command from salir which is spelled the same.
Nobody comes in here; Entrar third person present; Spanish says entrar en or entrar a never entrar plus a bare noun.
However it is not true; Masculine; on its own it means a seizure or trade embargo but sin embargo is a fixed phrase meaning however.
I want to listen to the music; Infinitive; escuchar is listening on purpose while oír is just hearing a sound.
My grandmother lives here; Feminine; the masculine is abuelo and los abuelos means the grandparents as a pair.
What did you all do?; Hacer third person plural preterite with the stem change to hic and no accent; hacían would be the imperfect.
It is on the floor; Masculine; el suelo is the floor or the ground outdoors while el piso is a floor of a building or a flat in Spain.
Can I see the photos?; Feminine la foto shortened from fotografía which is why it stays feminine despite the o ending.
Your brother is in prison; Feminine and the accent stays put in cárceles; Spanish uses en la cárcel with the article.
My mother always said that; Imperfect of decir which pairs naturally with siempre for habits; dijo would mean she said it once.
I am trying to sleep; Gerund of intentar; intentar plus a bare infinitive takes no preposition unlike tratar de dormir.
It is a family curse; Feminine; shouted alone it works as a mild damn in dubbed film speech but real speakers rarely say it.
I need a bit of quiet; Masculine; en silencio means silently and guardar silencio is to keep quiet.
My boss already left; Salir third person preterite with the accent on the o; salir con alguien also means to date someone.
See you at the club; Masculine borrowed word and the plural is los clubes; the final b is usually dropped so it sounds like clu.
I have to finish this; Infinitive; terminar and acabar are interchangeable here but acabar de plus infinitive means to have just done something.
I am afraid it is late; First person of temer; temer que takes the subjunctive and in speech tener miedo de is far more common.
It was just a joke; Feminine; you make a joke with hacer una broma and gastar una broma is to play a prank on someone.
The government does not tell the truth; Masculine and takes a singular verb unlike British English which says the government are.
I promise you; First person of prometer; the double pronoun order is always indirect then direct so te lo not lo te.
Look at the camera; Feminine; la cámara is also a chamber as in a legislative body and en cámara lenta means in slow motion.
Your mother called last night; Llamar third person preterite; llamar a alguien needs the personal a and llamarse is what your name is.
It is a gift for you; Masculine; the verb is regalar and de regalo means thrown in free.
They are all dead; Plural of muerto used as an adjective with estar because death is a state; un muerto as a noun means a dead man.
It is a heart attack; Masculine; ataque al corazón is the everyday phrase while doctors say infarto and un ataque de nervios is a panic attack.
Why don't you give me something?; Dar you-singular present; the yo form is doy and never do — dar is irregular only in the first person.
I'm here on business; Plural negocios covers business in general while singular negocio is one deal or one shop.
I wish I could help you; Past subjunctive of poder used for polite or unreal wishes; after si and ojalá Spanish needs this form where English says just could.
The plane already left; Masculine despite ending in -n; the accent moves in the plural aviones.
It's a police investigation; Feminine like all -ción nouns; the plural drops the accent — investigaciones.
It all ended well; Acabar he-she-it past; acabar de plus infinitive instead means to have just done something.
We have to keep quiet; Mantener conjugates exactly like tener — mantengo not manteno — and covers keeping something up as well as supporting a family.
My son is in the army; Masculine; it is the institution as a whole so Spanish says en el ejército where English drops the article.
I need a piece of paper; Masculine; the same word is an actor's role and un papel is one sheet since paper as material is uncountable.
It's in two parts; Feminine parte; the fixed phrase por otra parte means on the other hand not in another part.
I wouldn't say that; Conditional of decir built on the irregular stem dir-; the same form serves yo and él so the pronoun clears it up.
At first I didn't know; Masculine; al principio is a time expression meaning at the start and principio also means a moral principle.
Lieutenant we have a problem; Same form for a man or a woman — la teniente — and used bare as direct address without any article.
I have no desire at all; Masculine; the verb is desear so tener deseo de is the noun version of wanting something.
I don't want you to go; Present subjunctive of ir for tú; querer que forces the subjunctive whenever the two subjects differ.
The ship isn't working; Feminine; a nave is a large ship or spacecraft while barco is any ordinary boat.
Nobody leaves here; Salir he-she-it present; the yo form is salgo with a stray g and salir de is leaving a place while salir con is dating someone.
All this is garbage; Feminine and uncountable so never una basura; used freely for nonsense or bad work as well as actual trash.
There's no contact with the team; Masculine; ponerse en contacto con is the normal way to say get in touch with someone.
My husband died; Masculine partner of esposa; marido is more common in Spain while esposo sounds slightly formal everywhere.
The train arrived late; Masculine; you travel en tren with no article and the plural is trenes.
We didn't find anything; Encontrar we-form; present and past look identical here so context decides and nada after the verb still needs the earlier no.
He's the life of the party; Alma is feminine but takes el because it starts with stressed a — el alma buena and in the plural las almas.
I owe you an apology; Feminine noun from disculpar; pedir disculpas is to apologise while the bare disculpa also works as excuse me.
Walk carefully; Andar he-she-it present used as a command here; andar is walking around generally while ir is going somewhere specific.
Our marriage is over; Masculine; it is both the wedding institution and the married couple themselves.
This is madness; Feminine from loco; qué locura is the everyday exclamation for anything crazy.
She has a heart of gold; Masculine and uncountable; de oro is the way Spanish makes the adjective golden since there is no separate word.
Excuse me ma'am; Masculine; con permiso is what you say squeezing past someone not an apology like perdón.
I want to speak to the manager; Masculine; the feminine is la directora and the word covers a boss a school principal and a film director alike.
You're in danger; Masculine; the adjective is peligroso and estar en peligro uses estar because it is a temporary state.
Everyone wants freedom; Feminine like other -tad nouns; abstract so it usually drops the article after a verb.
I'm glad to see you; Alegrarse is reflexive so the me is obligatory; alegro without it would mean I cheer someone else up.
We'll have to wait; Future of tener on the irregular stem tendr-; tener que plus infinitive is the ordinary way to say have to.
It's on the right; Feminine noun for the right-hand side; derecho is a right or the law so keep the two apart.
Where is the hotel?; Encontrar he-she-it present; with se it means to be located and is more formal than está.
From head to toe; Plural of pie; Spanish runs the idiom feet first and a pie means on foot.
There's no room here; Masculine; espacio is physical room as well as outer space and for time you would say tiempo.
My grandfather was a teacher; Masculine; abuelos in the plural means grandparents of both genders not only grandfathers.
I didn't expect you here; Imperfect of esperar for yo or él; esperar is expecting waiting and hoping all in one verb.
What are you looking at?; Gerund of mirar; mirar is looking deliberately while ver is just seeing and no preposition follows it.
Health and money!; Feminine; salud is the toast you say clinking glasses and also what you say after a sneeze.
What a surprise to see you here!; Feminine; qué sorpresa takes no article unlike English which needs a.
I've thought about it a lot; Past participle of pensar; with haber it never changes ending and pensar en is thinking about while pensar que is believing.
He was my teacher; Masculine; maestro is a primary school teacher or a master of a craft while profesor teaches older students.
Go to hell; Masculine; irse al infierno keeps the article where English drops it and qué infierno describes any ordeal.
They could help us; Conditional of poder for they; it softens a suggestion while pudieron would state that they managed it.
Who are those guys?; Plural of tipo; for people it is informal for guys but un tipo de also means a kind of something.
My aunt lives in the city; Feminine of tío; in Spain tía doubles as slang for a woman the way tío means dude.
There was no crime; Masculine; crimen is a serious offence usually violent while a minor one is un delito.
Have we met before?; Past participle of conocer used with haber; conocer a alguien in the preterite or perfect means to meet someone for the first time.
The church is nearby; Feminine noun for the building and for the institution; Spanish says ir a la iglesia without an article change.
One more try; Masculine noun for an attempt; identical in spelling to intento meaning I try so word order tells you which one it is.
Most people; Feminine noun meaning the majority; it takes a singular verb even though it refers to many.
I give you my word; Irregular yo present of dar; the y ending shows up in doy voy soy estoy and nowhere else.
What did we do wrong?; Nosotros preterite of hacer on the stem hic- so never hacimos; the c keeps its soft s or th sound.
I love that scene; Feminine noun for a scene in a film or a place where something happened; la escena del crimen is the fixed phrase.
Is it in your flat?; Masculine noun meaning apartment in Spain and floor or storey elsewhere; Latin America usually says departamento for the home.
That is the signal; Feminine despite ending in a consonant; it covers signal sign and road sign but not a written notice.
It is quite an honour; Masculine noun; the h is silent so it sounds like onor.
The house is on fire; Feminine plural of llama meaning flame; spelled the same as llamas from llamar so context decides.
Open the door now; Third person present of abrir doubling as the tú command; the usted command is abra.
My brain is not working; Masculine noun; use it for the organ while mente is the mind you think with.
Did he really do it?; Only lives in the set phrase de veras meaning really; never use veras on its own.
I am watching the film; Gerund of ver and irregular since it is not veiendo; ver covers both seeing and watching.
She sets the table; Third person present of poner; the tú command drops to just pon.
I wonder why; Preguntar with the reflexive me means to wonder not to ask; plain pregunto is I ask.
It is in the kitchen; Feminine noun for kitchen and for cuisine; the identical cocina from cocinar means he cooks.
