Wedding dress; Masculine noun for a dress; it is also the participle of vestir so vestido de negro means dressed in black.
Whose horse is that?; Masculine noun; a mare is yegua and the plural caballos can mean horses in general.
They are coming this way; Third person plural present of venir; venir is movement toward the speaker while ir is away.
Lives are at stake; Plural of vida; en juego is the Spanish way of saying at stake.
See you at the bar; Masculine borrowed noun; in Spain a bar also serves coffee and food all day.
I need a haircut; El corte is a cut while la corte is a court or a royal court so the article changes the meaning.
What happened here?; Third person preterite of suceder; slightly more formal than pasó and it never means to succeed.
He does not take drugs; Feminine plural; la droga is a narcotic while medicine is medicamento or medicina.
The police are looking for you; Third person present of buscar; it already contains for so never add para or por after it.
I do not eat meat; Feminine noun for meat and for flesh; la carne de res is beef.
He seemed younger; Third person imperfect of parecer for how things looked over time; parecerse a means to resemble.
Where is his apartment?; Masculine noun meaning apartment across most of Latin America and department or government agency elsewhere.
Let us go to the sea; Normally masculine el mar though sailors and poets say la mar; playa is the beach itself.
Without doubt it is him; Feminine noun; the verb dudar keeps the same stem and no dudo que takes the subjunctive.
There is someone in the building; Masculine noun for a building as a structure; a house is casa and an office block is this.
I want to meet your mother; Conocer is being acquainted with people or places while saber is knowing facts; it needs the personal a before a person.
I am in charge here; Masculine noun; estar a cargo is to be in charge and un cargo is also a post or a criminal charge.
She is the victim; Always feminine la víctima even when the person is a man.
I have no energy today; Feminine noun for personal energy and for electrical power; the g sounds like a harsh h.
I am cold; Spanish has the cold with tener; hace frío is for the weather and estoy frío would mean your body is cold to the touch.
I am talking to my boss; Yo present of hablar; hablar con is to talk to someone and hablar de is to talk about something.
There is a dance tonight; Masculine noun for a dance or a ball; the art form is la danza.
My father works here; Third person present of trabajar; trabajar en is where you work and trabajar de is the job you do.
The mission is over; Feminine like almost every noun in ión; the plural adds es and drops the accent as misiones.
It is on the left; Feminine noun for the left side and for the political left; the z sounds like s in Latin America.
Do you want something to drink?; Infinitive of beber; tomar is the everyday word for having a drink in Latin America.
Put the weapon on the ground; Usted command of dejar and also its subjunctive; the tú command is deja.
I will give you an answer; Yo future of dar built on the short stem dar plus é so never daeré.
Did you know that?; Tú imperfect of saber for knowing something over a period; supiste would mean you found it out.
Call me when you can; Tú present subjunctive of poder; cuando about the future always takes the subjunctive.
He put the money there; Third person preterite of poner and irregular with no accent; puso not ponió.
He believed in you; Third person imperfect of creer for a lasting belief; creer en is to believe in and creer a is to believe what someone says.

When are you coming back?; Regresar is the plain verb for going back to a place and is the everyday choice in Latin America where Spain prefers volver; unlike volver it never means to do something again.
The train is arriving late; This is llegar for he she it or usted; the destination always needs a: llega a casa.
I can't understand a thing; Entender is grasping meaning; comprender is the more formal twin and saber is knowing a fact rather than following it.
Do you want to look at the photo?; Mirar is aiming your eyes on purpose while ver is just seeing; with people it takes a: mirar a tu padre.
I'm going to get the car out; Sacar is taking something out of somewhere and it swallows many English verbs: sacar una foto sacar dinero sacar la basura.
You've changed a lot; After haber the participle is frozen as cambiado; only when it works as an adjective does it agree: una vida cambiada.
Who's bringing dinner?; Traer moves something toward the speaker while llevar moves it away; the yo form is irregular: traigo.
In my opinion it's late; Opinión is feminine and the accent disappears in the plural: opiniones.
You'll see that it all works out; Future of ver for tú; in speech it is mostly reassurance or a way to open a story rather than a real prediction.
Hold on two seconds; Masculine and the same word as the ordinal second; in speech un segundo means any short moment.
One beer please; Cerveza is feminine; in a Spanish bar people order una caña for a small draft.
If he were here; Imperfect subjunctive of estar shared by yo and él; si plus this form marks something contrary to fact.
They don't believe me; Creer a alguien is believing a person while creer en is believing in something; no creo also does duty for I don't think so.
Can you hear that?; Oír is hearing that just reaches you; escuchar is choosing to listen; the forms are irregular: oigo oyes oye.
I'd have to talk with you; Conditional of tener and the same form for yo and él; tener que plus infinitive is the everyday way to say have to.
We haven't talked today; Participle of hablar; you talk con a person and de a topic and sobre for a subject at length.
We'll talk tomorrow; For -ar verbs the nosotros form is identical in the present and the preterite so only context tells you which; here the future sense comes from mañana.
The queen is here; Feminine partner of rey and also the queen in chess and cards.
That subject matters to me; Tema is masculine even though it ends in -a because it came from Greek: el tema los temas.
He spent two years in prison; Prisión is feminine and sounds institutional or legal while cárcel is the ordinary word for the building.
Nobody knows the reason why; As a noun it takes an article and a plural: los porqués; keep it apart from the question por qué and the answer porque.
I hope he comes back soon; Present subjunctive of volver for él or usted with the o turning into ue; espero que forces the subjunctive.
The audience is waiting; Singular and masculine even for a crowd; it is also an adjective and en público means in front of people.
What happened here?; Preterite of ocurrir for él; things ocurren while people hacen; se me ocurrió means an idea hit me.
We have to save the boy; Salvar is rescuing from danger; money you ahorras and a file you guardas.
Let's go watch the match; Masculine and it covers both a sports match and a political party.
He died because of the cold; Feminine; a causa de is the set phrase for because of and in court a causa is a case.
The sergeant isn't here; Masculine even for a woman: la sargento; ranks like this are used bare when you address someone.
Do you want to have dinner with me?; Spanish has one verb per meal so cenar replaces the whole phrase; the noun is la cena.
He's my coworker; Compañero and compañera cover colleague teammate and classmate; only context makes it romantic.
He took my car; Preterite of llevar for él; the reflexive llevarse means to make off with something and llevar takes things away while traer brings them here.
There's no other way; Existir for él; no existe flatly denies that a thing is real where no hay just says none is around.
I don't know this area; Feminine; zona is a part of a city or a stretch of land rather than a room-sized space.
It was his fate; Masculine and it does double duty for fate and for the place a trip ends.
The root of the problem; Base is feminine although it ends in -e; a base de means by means of and una base is also a military base.
He used to play here; Imperfect of soler for yo and él; the verb means to be in the habit of and is almost never used outside the present and the imperfect.
The customer is always right; One form for both genders: el cliente and la cliente; clienta is heard but not everywhere.
I have a meeting tomorrow; Masculine noun for a meeting or a run-in; it looks exactly like the yo form of encontrar.
Nobody found the money; Preterite of encontrar for él and the ue of encuentro is gone here; encontrarse con someone is bumping into them.
I don't want a fight; Feminine and it covers a shouting match as well as a real fistfight; it is also pelear for él.
We're heading north; Masculine; al norte de is the way to place something and the compass points stay lowercase.
I never wanted that; Preterite of querer for yo on the irregular stem quis-; no quise usually means I refused rather than I didn't feel like it.
The colonel gave the order; Masculine and unchanged for a woman: la coronel; one r in Spanish unlike the English spelling.
I bet you didn't know; Apostar for yo; apuesto que is a casual I bet that; as an adjective apuesto means good-looking.
Are you coming with us?; Venir for tú with the e turning into ie; venir is movement toward the speaker so answering a call you say voy not vengo.
They need help; Third person plural and also the ustedes form; necesitar takes its object bare with no preposition.
The tea is cold; Masculine and the accent is what separates it from the pronoun te; the plural is tés.
The trial was long; Masculine; besides a trial it means judgement or sanity as in perder el juicio.
I hope we can go; Present subjunctive of poder for nosotros; espero que and para que both pull this form.
Where's my key?; Feminine; cerrar con llave is to lock and in much of Latin America a llave is also a tap or a wrench.
You're wrong; Past participle of equivocarse used as an adjective with estar; Spanish says you "are mistaken" as a state so it agrees in gender - equivocada to a woman.
What's your position?; Feminine like almost every -ción noun; used for physical location and for a stance in an argument or a job rank.
My back hurts; Feminine and normally singular for one person's back; it is the back of a body while respaldo is the back of a chair.
It was a real success; Masculine and never means "exit" - that false friend trips up English speakers; tener éxito is the way to say to succeed.
I'm going anyway; Plural of modo; de todos modos is a fixed filler meaning anyway or in any case and the plural is obligatory there.
Open the window; Feminine; it is a window in a wall while a shop window is escaparate or vidriera.
Let's see what happens; Present subjunctive of ver used as a we-command; as an interjection it softens into a thoughtful "let's see" or "well now".
It's some kind of joke; Feminine despite ending in -e; una especie de is the everyday way to say "a sort of" and separately it means a biological species.
We didn't have any money; Tener we-form imperfect for an ongoing past situation; the preterite tuvimos would mean we got money at one moment.
There's no difference; Feminine; the verb is not "hacer diferencia" - use no importa or da igual for "it makes no difference".
There are many ways; Plural of forma; here it means ways or methods rather than shapes and de todas formas parallels de todos modos.
I want to ask a favor; Pedir is asking for something you want while preguntar is asking a question; it stem-changes to pido and pide.
Give me an example; Masculine; por ejemplo is the standard "for example" and dar el ejemplo is to set an example.
Listen to the radio; Feminine when it means the broadcast or set even though it ends in -o; el radio is a radius or in some countries the device itself.
We have to stay calm; Feminine noun not an adjective; ¡calma! on its own works as "easy now" and calmarse is the reflexive verb.
There's no place like home; Masculine and warmer than casa - it is the household or hearth rather than the building.
I'll be back tomorrow; Volver I-form future; the stem stays volv- so no o-to-ue change happens in the future tense.
It's at the bottom of the sea; Masculine; it covers the bottom of something and also the back of a room and en el fondo means "deep down".
We'll go by train; Ir we-form future built on the irregular ir- stem; note vamos alone often serves as the future in speech.
They had already left; Haber they-form imperfect for the pluperfect; pair it with a participle and never with an infinitive.
It's not from this planet; Masculine despite the -a ending like problema and tema because of its Greek origin.
Regarding that; Masculine and only appears in the phrases con respecto a and al respecto; do not confuse it with respeto meaning esteem.
I await your return; Masculine noun from regresar; commoner in Latin America where vuelta or regreso both work and estar de regreso means to be back.
Due to the bad weather; Participle of deber but here fixed in debido a meaning "because of"; the a is required.
I'll be your friend; Ser I-form future on the irregular ser- stem; ser is used for lasting identity so a role like friend takes ser not estar.
They were right; Tener they-form imperfect; tener razón is "to have reason" where English uses to be so never estar for being right.
I want to read that book; Regular -er infinitive but its participle leído and preterite leyó carry accents and a y.
I can't stop; Parar is stopping motion or activity while dejar de means to quit doing something; parada is the noun for a bus stop.
I left the key here; Dejar I-form preterite; dejar is leaving an object behind while salir is a person leaving a place.
I have a lot of respect for you; Masculine; Spanish uses tener respeto a alguien and faltar el respeto is to be disrespectful.
I'm going to write a letter; Regular -ir verb but the participle is the irregular escrito; escribir a is to write to a person.
See you at the station; Feminine like other -ción nouns; it also means a season of the year and estación de policía is a police station.
She asked me for help; Pedir he-she preterite with the e-to-i change; the thing requested follows directly with no preposition.
I don't have a single clue; Feminine; a clue or lead and also a track or runway and dance floor - context decides.
You're a star; Feminine even for a man; it covers stars in the sky and celebrities just as in English.
My son is sick; Works as adjective and as noun for a patient; illness is a temporary state so it takes estar not ser.
My head hurts; Doler he-she present with the o-to-ue change; it works like gustar - the body part is the subject and you are the indirect object.
I don't believe in dreams; Plural of sueño; the same word means sleep so tengo sueño is I'm sleepy not I have a dream.
We'll see about that; Ver we-form future; as a set reply it signals polite doubt rather than a real plan to look.
Those are the captain's orders; Plural of orden and feminine in the sense of a command; masculine el orden means tidiness or sequence.
I'm very busy right now; Participle of ocupar used as an adjective with estar; it also describes a taken seat or an engaged phone line.
Run — the police are coming; Correr he-she present doubling as the tú command; for -er verbs the tú command and the third person look identical.
I haven't been able to sleep; Irregular participle of poder; use it only with haber and keep pude for a completed one-off attempt.
Don't leave me here; Present subjunctive of dejar for a negative tú command; the plain dejas would be wrong after no.
It's another level; Masculine with plural niveles; otro nivel is common slang praise and a nivel de meaning "at the level of" is widely criticized in careful writing.
Have you all seen my brother?; Haber you-plural present used only in Spain; Latin America says han visto with ustedes.
We need someone with experience; Feminine; it covers both know-how and a single episode you lived through.
Where's the exit?; Feminine noun from salir; also a departure time and dar la salida is to start a race.
You can trust me; Confiar takes en for trusting a person and it stem-splits into confío and confías with an accent.
That was what I needed; Necesitar imperfect and identical for yo and él so context or a pronoun tells you who.
You and I are brothers; Hermano is masculine and the plural hermanos covers a mixed group of siblings; only all-female groups take hermanas.
Where are my shoes?; El zapato is masculine and you buy them by the par; the singular is used for one shoe only.
What colour is it?; Color is masculine even though nouns in -or often look otherwise; Spanish asks de qué color rather than what colour.
Just a quick look; Vistazo lives almost entirely in echar or dar un vistazo; alone it means a glance not a stare.
I am going to try; Tratar de plus infinitive is to try; tratar a alguien is to treat a person; without de it is not "to try about".
In my view it is late; Here parecer is a noun meaning opinion; a mi parecer is fixed and does not take de.
The judge is not in; Juez is masculine but is used for women too; the plural is jueces and the feminine jueza is newer.
The patient is not talking; Paciente has one form for both genders so only el or la marks sex; it is also the adjective patient.
I hope you have seen it; Hayas is the tú present subjunctive of haber and is forced by espero que; the indicative has would be wrong here.
Do you have a bag?; Bolsa is feminine; capitalised la Bolsa is the stock exchange and in Spain a handbag is a bolso.
This is not art; Arte is masculine in the singular yet feminine in the plural as in las bellas artes.
The kids are playing; Jugando is the gerund of jugar and covers games and sport; playing an instrument is tocar.
How long have you been here?; Llevas is llevar for tú; llevar plus a time span replaces English present perfect; it also means to carry or to wear.
I am glad to see you; Alegra works backwards from English since the pleasing thing is the subject; me alegro de is the reflexive alternative.
Do you want to dance with me?; Bailar is the plain verb to dance and takes con for a partner; the noun baile is the dance itself.
The devil exists; Diablo is masculine; the plural in ¿qué diablos? is just an exclamation and has no religious sense.
I did not hear anything; Oí is the yo preterite of oír and needs the accent; oír is passive hearing while escuchar is deliberate listening.
I do not think he knows anything; Sepa is the present subjunctive of saber on the irregular stem sep- and serves yo usted él and ella.
We are heading south; Sur is masculine and takes el; direction is al sur or hacia el sur not just sur.
The band has arrived; Banda is feminine and covers a music group and a criminal gang; banda sonora is a soundtrack.
I want to learn to dance; Aprender needs a before an infinitive; aprender de memoria is to learn by heart.
What is the price?; Precio is masculine; a mitad de precio means half price and precioso is unrelated meaning lovely.
I do not feel like it; Ganas is feminine plural and the singular gana is rare; tener ganas de plus infinitive is the everyday way to say you feel like doing something.
We had a problem; Tuvimos is tener for nosotros in the preterite with the irregular tuv- stem; teníamos would describe an ongoing situation instead.
She came back home last night; Volvió is volver for él or ella in the preterite; volver a plus infinitive means to do something again.
These are my books; Libro is masculine; a librería sells books while a library is a biblioteca.
One of my eyes hurts; Ojo is masculine and ¡Ojo! shouted alone means watch out.
It must be about three; Serán is the future of ser for ellos and ustedes; Spanish uses this future to guess at the time rather than to predict.
Good heavens! What happened?; The plural cielos is only an exclamation; singular cielo means sky or heaven and is also a pet name.
I have not killed anyone; Matado is the participle of matar used after haber; muerto is the participle you use for dying not for killing.
At your orders commander; Comandante has one form for both genders; it is a military rank and also what you call an airline captain.
We need action; Acción is feminine and its plural acciones drops the accent; in finance una acción is a share.
Those are the rules; Regla is feminine and also means a ruler for drawing and colloquially a period.
It is a work of art; Obra is feminine and covers an artwork a stage play and a building site; the road sign obras means roadworks.
There is still hope; Esperanza is the feminine noun from esperar which itself blurs hoping waiting and expecting.
It is a matter of time; Cuestión is feminine and means issue or matter; a question you actually ask is una pregunta.
It does not bother me; Molesta puts the annoying thing as the subject just like gusta; it never carries the English sense of molest.
We are having problems; Teniendo is the gerund of tener; Spanish rarely puts tener in the progressive except with events like problems or a baby.
I need the report; Informe is masculine; the adjective informe means shapeless and the verb is informar.
The river is cold; Río is masculine and the accent separates it from rio the preterite of reír.
Can you open the door?; Abrir is regular in the present but its participle is the irregular abierto.
I promise not to touch anything; Tocar is to touch and also to play an instrument; me toca a mí means it is my turn.
I am going to tell you something; Contar means both to count and to tell a story; contar con alguien is to rely on them.
I am still here; Sigo is seguir for yo with the e to i change; seguir plus a gerund means to keep on doing something.
It is inside; As a noun interior is masculine and means the inside; ropa interior is underwear.
Is this your flat?; Apartamento is the usual word in much of Latin America while Spain says piso and Mexico departamento.
Let nobody see me; Vea is the present subjunctive of ver for él ella and usted and doubles as the usted command.
Where are you all?; Estáis is the vosotros form of estar used only in Spain; Latin America says están even to friends.
Money does not worry me; Preocupa makes the worrying thing the subject; to say you worry about something use me preocupo por.
He took my hand; Tomó is tomar for él or ella in the preterite; tomar means to take and also to drink so tomar algo is to have a drink.
The film starts now; Third person present of empezar with the e turning into ie; to start doing something you need empezar a plus an infinitive.
That is how the war began; Third person preterite of empezar; the z hardens to c in the yo form empecé so the sound stays the same.
I want them to go home; Present subjunctive of ir for they or ustedes; it doubles as the ustedes command so ¡vayan! is get going.
Someone is knocking; Llamar covers phoning and naming and knocking; llaman with no subject is the normal way to say somebody is at the door.
Sorry about my mistake; The tú command of perdonar and the casual sorry you use with a friend; with usted it becomes perdone.
I will be back in two minutes; Yo present of volver with o becoming ue; volver a plus infinitive means to do a thing again.
It was a stroke of luck; Masculine and means a blow or knock; de golpe means all of a sudden and un golpe de estado is a coup.
I have finished my work; Participle of acabar and fixed after haber; estar acabado said of a person means washed up rather than done.
I like his style; Masculine; it means manner as much as fashion and algo por el estilo is how you say something along those lines.
Can we meet up tomorrow?; In Spain quedar is arranging to meet; it also means to be left over as in queda poco and quedarse is to stay.
I have two letters for you; Plural of the feminine carta; the same word covers letters you post and playing cards so only context tells you which.
There is a bomb here!; Feminine; it also means a pump for water and in Spain pasarlo bomba is to have a great time.
He has a gun in his hand; Feminine and means a handgun specifically while arma is any weapon at all.
I want to taste the food; Probar is tasting or trying out and also proving something; probarse with the pronoun is trying clothes on.
Whatever your majesty says; Majestad is feminine so it is su majestad even for a king although adjectives agree with the monarch's own sex — su majestad está preocupado.
Can you bring the coffee?; Traer is bringing towards the speaker while llevar is taking away; the yo form is irregular traigo.
The car is running; Feminine; estar en marcha means up and running or underway and in Spain irse de marcha is going out at night.
My flight leaves at two; Masculine noun from volar; it is spelled exactly like vuelo meaning I fly so the article is what marks it as a noun.
I left you a note; Feminine; the same word is a school grade and a musical note; se nota que belongs to the verb notar instead.
We will be here tomorrow; Future of estar for we on the regular stem estar-; it is about place or state so seremos would be wrong here.
It has no value at all; Masculine and covers both worth in money and courage; tener valor is to be brave rather than to be worth.
What is the goal?; Masculine; it is a goal or target and also a camera lens; as an adjective it means unbiased.
Suddenly he said something; Repente survives only inside the fixed phrase de repente and is never used on its own.
He owed my boss money; Third person imperfect of deber; besides owing it carries should have as in debía saberlo so context decides.
Who will go to the party?; Future of ir for he she or usted; the stem stays ir- and only the accented ending changes.
I do not have the ticket; Feminine; it is a ticket for a show and also an entrance or way in; travel tickets are billetes not entradas.
I will not leave you alone; Future of dejar for I; dejar is leaving something behind or allowing and dejar de plus infinitive is to quit doing.
I want to avoid trouble; Evitar is avoiding or preventing; no pude evitarlo is I could not help it and evitar que takes the subjunctive.
This machine is broken; Feminine; escribir a máquina means to type and una máquina de café is a coffee maker.
My neck hurts; Masculine and also the collar of a shirt; with body parts Spanish uses el not a possessive like my.
I met your sister yesterday; Preterite of conocer for I and it means met for the first time; the imperfect conocía means already knew her.
Those were different times; Plural of tiempo meaning eras or periods; time as a quantity stays singular so mucho tiempo never becomes muchos tiempos.
I hope he takes the train; Present subjunctive of tomar for he she or usted and also the usted command; ¡tome! offered with the hand means here you are.
The animals are hungry; Masculine plural of animal formed with -es; called of a person it means a brute so no seas animal is do not be an oaf.
If I had more time; Imperfect subjunctive of tener; after si it sets up something unreal and pairs with a conditional like tendría.
He came with his partner; Feminine even when the partner is a man; it means both a couple and one member of it and en pareja is as a couple.
This summer we will go to the sea; Masculine; with seasons you say en verano with no article and el verano only when you point at a specific one.
One day you will be the boss; Future of ser for tú; it also voices a guess or a jab as in ¡serás tonto! meaning what a fool you are.
That is a lie; Feminine; parece mentira means it is hard to believe and the person who tells them is a mentiroso.
I want to pay by card; Feminine and covers a bank card or a greeting card; con tarjeta drops the article; playing cards are cartas.
Let them do their job; Present subjunctive of hacer for they built on the hago stem; as an ustedes command hagan el favor is please do.
I lost my phone yesterday; Preterite of perder for I; the ie of pierdo disappears in the past and perderse means to get lost.
Do you want to go running with me?; Correr is to run and also what time or news does when it passes or spreads; in Spain correrse is vulgar.
Who brought this?; Participle of traer; the i takes an accent so it is heard as its own syllable and never agrees after haber.
When my father arrives; Present subjunctive of llegar with a u added to keep the g hard; cuando about the future always takes the subjunctive.
My brother wears my clothes; Third person of usar which covers using a thing and wearing clothes; se usa is the way to say one uses.
I am going to try something; Intentar takes an infinitive with no preposition while tratar needs de; intentar is attempting and probar is testing.
These flowers are for you; Plural of la flor which adds -es; flor is feminine even though it does not end in a.
It is starting to scare me; Gerund of dar; dar miedo is the normal way to say something is frightening and estar dando puts it in this moment.
I have no other choice; Feminine like every noun in -ción and the plural loses the accent as opciones.
We are on an island; Feminine noun; and Spanish says en una isla where English says on an island.
Close the door please; This is cerrar for he/she or the usted command; the e becomes ie when stressed so yo cierro but nosotros cerramos.
I love your skin; Feminine despite ending in a consonant; it also means hide or leather in the sense of the material.
He is not my enemy; Masculine; a woman is la enemiga and Spanish uses ser here because it is identity not a passing state.
I am leaving the money here for you; Dejar is to leave something behind; use salir or irse when a person leaves a place.
We are still young; Plural of joven and the accent appears only in the plural to keep the stress; it works as noun or adjective.
Have you ordered the food?; Past participle of pedir which is asking for a thing; preguntar is asking a question.
My mother does not understand anything; Entender for he/she/usted; the double negative no plus nada is required in Spanish.
I want justice for my son; Feminine and used without an article after verbs like querer; el juez comes from the same family.
Nobody wakes me up in the morning; Despertar for he/she; with a reflexive pronoun me despierto means I wake up by myself.
I am only asking for a little peace; Pedir for yo with the e turning into i; unlike decir it adds no g so pido never becomes pigo.
It is so hot in here!; Masculine noun meaning heat and Spanish says hace calor with hacer for weather and tengo calor for a person.
The city lights; Plural of luz where the z turns to c before es; feminine.
I am not talking about you; Referirse always takes a pronoun plus a and is the normal way to say I mean; not the verb for meaning of words.
Yesterday we went to the party; Preterite we form of ir; identical to the preterite of ser so context decides between we went and we were.
The battle is over; Feminine; a batalla is one fight inside a guerra which is the whole war.
She is trying to help; Intentar for he/she and it is followed straight by the infinitive with no preposition; tratar needs de.
My arm hurts; Masculine; Spanish uses the article el and not a possessive for body parts.
I want him to leave my house; Present subjunctive of salir built on the yo form salgo; querer que always forces the subjunctive.
I cannot remember his name; Infinitive of recordar; acordarse de is the everyday alternative and needs the pronoun.
We have to escape from here; Infinitive; escapar takes de before the place and often appears as escaparse.
Gentlemen there is a problem; Plural of señor with no accent since señores is already stressed correctly; used to address a group politely.
Only two minutes are left; Quedar for they meaning to remain; quedarse with a pronoun means to stay somewhere.
I cannot feel my legs; Feminine plural of pierna; the leg of a table is la pata not la pierna.
I have a visitor tomorrow; Feminine and it covers both the visit and the person visiting regardless of their gender.
What are you using?; Gerund of usar; for wearing clothes Spanish prefers llevar though usar is heard in Latin America.
We have won the game; Past participle of ganar which covers winning and earning money.
Do not make any movement; Masculine; also used for a political or artistic movement.
In spite of everything I love you; A pesar de is a fixed phrase for in spite of; the same word as the verb to weigh so think of weight bearing down.
I am on holiday; Feminine and always plural; estar de vacaciones is the fixed phrase for being away.
Who has taken my car?; Past participle of tomar; tomar covers taking and drinking while llevar is taking something somewhere.
Where had you been?; Haber in the imperfect for tú; it only builds compound tenses so it never stands alone as had.
Do you have plans tonight?; Masculine plural of plan; the singular has no accent and neither does the plural.
Let us go to the movies tonight; Masculine; el cine is both the building and the art form and there is no plural in this sense.
Now it is your turn; Tocar for he/she; besides touching and playing an instrument tocarle a alguien means it is that person's turn.
I do not trust him; Feminine; tener confianza en is how you say to trust and con confianza means openly.
I do not remember their names; Masculine plural of nombre; el nombre is the first name and el apellido is the surname.
Wait here a moment; Present subjunctive of esperar used as the ustedes command; esperar covers waiting and hoping.
Where are my trousers?; Masculine and normally plural for one garment; the singular pantalón carries an accent that the plural drops.
That is not a defence; Feminine even when it refers to a male defender on a team.
The party ended early; Terminar preterite for he/she and the accent on the o marks the past; without it termino means I finish.
He has left the house; Past participle of salir and it is regular; salir de means to leave a place.
I feel a lot of pressure; Feminine like other nouns in ión; the plural presiones loses the accent.
We have a witness; Masculine but it stays testigo for a woman too; only the article changes to la.
They should call the police; Deber in the conditional for they; the conditional softens it to should while deben means they must.
I have forgotten everything; Past participle of olvidar; olvidarse de with the pronoun is just as common in speech.
The soldiers are here; Masculine plural; a mixed group still takes the masculine form.
It turns out you were right; Resultar for he/she and resulta que is the set phrase for it turns out that.
It all depends on you; Depender always takes de where English uses on.
There is no reason; Masculine; motivo is the reason or grounds for doing something while razón is being right or a reason in argument.
Can you speak English?; Languages are masculine and stay lowercase in Spanish; the accent drops in inglesa and ingleses.
He's in the study; This is the noun for a study room or a recording studio; los estudios means someone's schooling.
This has to end; Acabar is terminar with a plainer feel; acabar de plus infinitive means to have just done something and acabar con means to wipe out.
I don't understand my feelings; Masculine; un sentimiento is an emotion while el sentido is a meaning or a sense.
What are you drinking?; Gerund of tomar; with a glass in hand tomar is to drink and estar plus gerund pins it to this very moment.
They gave me the job; Ellos preterite of dar; it borrows the -ir endings and carries no accent so dieron never daron.
They look like brothers; Parecer is to seem or look like; add se and parecerse a means to physically resemble someone.
Where are my keys?; La llave is feminine and also names a faucet or a wrench.
The dogs are outside; The masculine plural covers a mixed pack; perras is the feminine and is an insult aimed at people.
What's the purpose?; Masculine; a propósito is the everyday phrase and means either on purpose or by the way.
Have you heard the news?; Feminine and countable so una noticia is one single item; the plural noticias is the news on TV.
We're leaving now; Partir is to depart or to split something; the form you hear most is a partir de meaning starting from.
It's ten metres away; Masculine; el metro is also the subway and the abbreviation m takes no period.
There are no customers today; Cliente ends in -e for both sexes so el or la does the work; clienta exists but sounds dated.
Nobody will be able to get in; Future of poder for él or usted on the short stem podr-; it often softens a guess rather than stating a fact.
This is ridiculous; It works as adjective and noun; hacer el ridículo is to make a fool of yourself and it agrees as ridícula.
Ladies and gentlemen; Dama is formal and ceremonial where señoras is what you say daily; las damas is also the game of checkers.
The operation was a success; Feminine and it covers surgery as well as a police or military job; the accent vanishes in operaciones.
My son doesn't eat a thing; Third person present of comer and also the tú command; in Spain comer on its own means to have lunch.
My father owns a business; Feminine; empresa is a firm as a business venture while compañía leans to the legal company.
Let's go to the lab; Masculine and never clipped the way English says lab; stress falls on the -to-.
It was your choice; Feminine; singular is a choice and the plural elecciones is a political election.
Give me a kiss; Masculine noun behind the verb besar; dos besos is the normal greeting in Spain and the way to sign off a message.
Listen to this conversation; Feminine with plural conversaciones; a casual chat is una charla in Spain and una plática in Mexico.
Come into my arms; Masculine; keep brazos apart from armas since one is arms on your body and the other is weapons.
The spirit is still here; Masculine even though it ends in -u; it also means a ghost and the plural is espíritus.
Why won't you leave me alone?; Tú present of dejar; dejar is to leave something behind or to let someone do a thing and dejar de plus infinitive is to quit doing it.
I'm not interested at all; It behaves like gustar so the topic is the subject and you say me interesa; yo interesa is wrong.
I have faith in you; Feminine and about as short as a Spanish noun gets; de buena fe means in good faith and the plural is never used.
She never shows fear; Mostrar changes o to ue when stressed so muestra not mostra; enseñar is the more casual way to show something.
It's a trap; Feminine; hacer trampa is to cheat at a game so the word covers trickery as well as traps.
I have no memory of that; Feminine and it names the faculty itself; one particular memory is un recuerdo.
It's exactly the opposite; Lo contrario is the opposite and al contrario is on the contrary; as a noun it also means the opponent.
My son is a soldier; It ends in -o yet a woman is la soldado; after ser a profession drops the article.
Can I come up?; Subir is to go up and also to get into a car or to upload a file; its opposite is bajar.
It's my turn; Masculine; besides your turn in a game it means a work shift as in turno de noche.
I'd love to go; Conditional of encantar in the gustar pattern; it is the polite way to accept an invitation.
See you at the restaurant; Masculine and it keeps a final -e that English dropped; plural restaurantes.
He's leaving right now; Gerund of salir; estar saliendo con alguien is how you say two people are dating.
Thanks for the welcome; Feminine as a noun; used as a greeting it agrees with the arrival so bienvenido bienvenida or bienvenidos.
You're going to fall; Caer is to fall but a person tripping normally uses caerse; the yo form is caigo and me cae bien means I like someone.
I'll take you home; Yo future of llevar; llevar carries something away from where you are while traer brings it toward you.
There's no milk; Feminine; in Spain ¡la leche! is a shout of surprise and tener mala leche is being in a foul mood.
Look at the stars; Feminine; it covers film stars and hotel ratings just as in English.
I prefer coffee; Yo present of preferir with e turning into ie; an infinitive follows it bare as in prefiero ir.
Is the network working?; Feminine; it means a net and a network and la red is also the internet.
Excuse me sir; Usted command of oír and the normal way to flag down a stranger or a waiter; oye is the tú version.
I hope they're all right; Present subjunctive of estar for ellos or ustedes; the accent is required and phrases like espero que force this mood.
We have bills to pay; Feminine plural of cuenta for bills or bank accounts; it is also the tú form of contar and darse cuenta means to realize.
I'm going to call a taxi; Masculine with plural taxis; the driver is un taxista across Latin America.
That ring is my mother's; Masculine; it is any ring including a wedding one; anillo de boda where English says wedding band.
I don't want to ask again; Preguntar is asking a question while pedir is asking for a thing; you preguntar por a person to ask after them.
The victory is ours; Feminine; also a woman's name so capitalization is what tells them apart in writing.
I'm no hero; Masculine and the accent stays on the e in the plural héroes; a woman is la heroína.
I've already decided; Past participle of decidir so it never changes for gender after he; decidirse a hacer algo is making up your mind to do it.
I don't like those movies; Feminine plural; película is also the physical film or a thin layer like the film on milk.
Who's in charge?; One form for both genders: el responsable and la responsable; as an adjective it also means reliable.
I need a drink; Masculine; a trago is a swallow or a shot of alcohol while bebida is any drink; pasar un mal trago is a rough time.
She'll come back tomorrow; Future of volver for él or ella; the ue never appears in the future because the stem is unstressed.
He's behind the tree; Masculine; the plural árboles keeps the written accent on the á even though it adds a syllable.
The boy has no teeth; Masculine plural of diente; teeth are dientes but a molar is muela and toothache is dolor de muelas.
A truck came by here; Masculine; the accent drops in the plural camiones; in Mexico a camión is also a city bus.
I don't want to sell the house; Vender is selling and comprar is buying; se vende on a sign is what English calls for sale.
I want him to call me; Present subjunctive of llamar for él or usted; querer que always forces this form and never the infinitive.
We have to fight; Luchar is struggling or fighting for a cause while pelear is a physical scrap; luchar por is what you fight for.
The corporal said nothing; Masculine; it is also a cape of land and the end of something: al fin y al cabo means after all.
What's that noise?; Masculine; hacer ruido is to make noise and a rumour is also un ruido in some regions.
The fight isn't over; Feminine; it covers a struggle or a movement as well as wrestling as a sport.
Nobody dies today; Morir for él with o turning into ue; morirse de risa or de hambre is the everyday exaggerated use.
My watch isn't working; Masculine; the same word is a clock and a wristwatch and the plural is relojes.
The cat is on the table; Masculine and a female cat is la gata; a gato is also a car jack.
We're going to find out the truth; Averiguar is finding something out by digging while encontrar is simply finding; the u is pronounced in averiguar.
I'm afraid of flying; Volar is flying and the o becomes ue in vuelo; it also means to blow something up.
Will your father come?; Future of venir on the irregular stem vendr-; do not confuse it with vender forms like venderá.
He ran out of the house; Gerund of correr; salir corriendo is the normal way to say to rush out rather than a separate verb.
I'm still going to class; Gerund of ir and completely irregular since iendo would be wrong; seguir plus gerund is to keep on doing something.
My daughter goes to school; Masculine; a colegio is usually a primary or secondary school often private while universidad is higher up.
It doesn't make a sound; Masculine; sonido is a sound in general and ruido is an unwanted one; volume on a device is el sonido too.
He's a real gentleman; Masculine; originally a horseman from caballo and now a gentleman; on a door it marks the men's room.
I don't know the code; Masculine; it is a PIN or a legal code alike and the accent is on the first o.
What do you want us to do?; Present subjunctive of hacer for nosotros built on hag-; hagamos alone works as a let's do it.
I can't see the picture; Feminine despite ending in n and the plural shifts the accent to imágenes.
It's not worth the risk; Masculine; correr un riesgo is to take a risk and arriesgar is the verb.
We're home; Llegar for nosotros and identical in the preterite so context decides; llegar a is arriving somewhere with no preposition like English's at.
Is there bread at home?; Masculine and uncountable in normal use so un pan is a loaf; ser pan comido is to be dead easy.
It's worth a million dollars; Masculine and unlike cien it needs de before the noun: un millón de personas; the plural is millones.
The lady wants to talk to you; Feminine; dama is formal or old-fashioned where mujer or señora is everyday; it is also the queen in cards.
I want water with ice; Masculine and uncountable so no un; romper el hielo works just like breaking the ice.
He fell in the street; Preterite of caer for él with the y and the accent; caerse with se is the normal way to say to fall over.
The press already knows; Feminine and singular even though it means all the journalists; it is also a press machine.
They avenge his death; Vengar for ellos meaning to avenge; it looks exactly like the subjunctive of venir so only the sentence tells you which verb.
I'd rather walk; Caminar is walking and andar overlaps but also means to go about or to function; dar un paseo is to go for a stroll.
There's nothing on TV; Feminine; the set itself is often el televisor and Spanish says en la televisión where English says on TV.
Nothing will happen; Future of pasar for él; pasar covers happening as well as passing so qué pasará is what will happen.
There are moments like that; Masculine plural; en este momento is right now and por el momento is for the time being.
Can I take your car?; In Spain coger is the ordinary verb for taking or catching but in much of Latin America it is vulgar so tomar or agarrar is safer.
There's a chance; Feminine like most nouns in dad; the plural is posibilidades and it also means the means to do something.
I wish he had come; Imperfect subjunctive of haber for él and hubiera is equally correct; it builds the past unreal as in si hubiese sabido.
That's my seat; Masculine; from sentarse so it is also the seat of a chair; tomar asiento is a polite have a seat.
The project is finished; Masculine; the y sounds like a soft consonant here and proyectar is to project or to plan.
